Allied forces began to field Matildas in 1940. The concept behind this British infantry tank was a strengthened armor at the cost of speed and firepower. Indeed, the German 37mm AT-guns were unable to penetrate the Matilda's armor, but weak armament and low mobility of these tanks made them poor performers in tank duels, mainly relegating them to infantry support role.

The Daimler was developed in 1939 and was considered the most successful British wheeled armored car of the WWII. The welded hull with good slope angles protected the crew from bullets and fragments, while the six-cylinder carburettor engine and all-wheeled drive provided the vehicle with great speed and manoeuvrability. The fully revolving turret was equipped with a machine gun and a 40mm cannon to combat lightly-armored targets.

This British infantry tank that entered service in 1940 due to its weight of 16 tonnes could be considered light, yet its armor surpassed some medium tanks. "Valentine" was distinguished by simple construction and reliability of its engine, but had weak armament that was unable to deal with most enemy tanks. Was widely used on all fronts for infantry support role.

Mass production of the 20-tonne Crusader cruiser tank began in 1940. This highly mobile and well-armored vehicle made its first appearance in North Africa, posing a real threat to Rommel's Afrikakorps. The 1942 modification featured a 57mm gun with armor-piercing rounds capable of destroying almost any tank at that time. However, its efficiency was reduced when Germany adopted newer and heavier armored vehicles.

Perhaps one of Great Britain's most original military projects was developed in the 1930s by Vickers-Armstrong Limited as a typical cruiser tank. Tetrarchs were distinguished by their high mobility, steering and extremely low weight which allowed this vehicle to be used in airborne operations. The armor-piercing rounds of the tank's 40mm gun were effective against light enemy vehicles. However, its own light armor couldn't protect its crew from high-calibre bullets.

Adopted by the British Army in 1920, this 3-inch infantry mortar was often used to provide fire support to attacking and defending infantry. The gun had a high rate of fire and its simple design allowed for the shortest time to firing under artificial or natural cover.

Mass production of the Nashorn tank destroyer started in February 1943 and continued until the end of the war. Its 88mm gun left almost no chances to enemy tanks. That, combined with its great mobility, made the "Rhinoceros" a fearsome weapon. Its frontal armor was thick enough, but the open fighting compartment and almost vertical side armor plates did not provide sufficient protection to the crew.

This rocket artillery launcher came into being in June 1944 and, thanks to its successful design, was soon widely used among Wehrmacht troops, displacing other models of similar German guns. A framework with guide rails for 300mm rockets was mounted on a wheeled carriage and the rockets, which detonated after launching, produced a tremendous destructive force, damaging fortifications and causing heavy losses to enemy infantry and equipment.

This 20mm flak autocannon was developed in Sweden and became the most widely used anti-aircraft gun of WWII. The ease of use and high rate of fire contributed to its popularity - in 1939 it was fielded by the British Armed Forces, and in 1941 by the US Navy. Oerlikons were used against both aerial and ground targets and were effective against infantry and lightly-armored vehicles.

The PaK 35 artillery gun was used to engage enemy vehicles, destroy weapon emplacements and eliminate non-sheltered personnel. A semi-automatic sliding-wedge breechblock provided the gun with high rate of fire, while armor-piercing rounds easily defeated the lightly-armored vehicles of the time at medium ranges. During early stages of WWII, the gun was issued to Wehrmacht infantry divisions as the main anti-tank weapon, however, as tank armor thickened, it became ineffective.

The self-propelled Bison Sturmpanzer I entered service with the German Army in 1940. It was basically a heavy 150mm sIG-33 gun mounted atop the base of a Pz.I was. The artillery gun was mainly used to destroy fortifications and heavily-defended areas. Its armor plates partially protected the crew from shrapnels and bullets, but were unable to provide them cover from artillery fire.

First guns of this type appeared during the spring of 1942 on the Eastern Front. The PaK 40 was designed to deal with tanks and armored vehicles, however, its fairly large calibre and availability of high-explosive rounds allowed it to be used to suppress weapon emplacements, demolish light fortifications and eliminate enemy personnel. Its accuracy and effective range exceed that of the Soviet ZIS-3 field artillery gun.

On the basis of the obsolete 18-pounder guns, British engineers developed a 25-pounder gun-howitzer which was able to fire 11kg high explosive shells at great distances. Its telescopic sights were of great use in direct fire against enemy tanks, while the large shield plate protected the crew from bullets and fragments. The gun showed excellent performance on the battlefield, earning respect for its range and impressive destructive ability.

On the basis of the obsolete 18-pounder guns, British engineers developed a 25-pounder gun-howitzer which was able to fire 11kg high explosive shells at great distances. Its telescopic sights were of great use in direct fire against enemy tanks, while the large shield plate protected the crew from bullets and fragments. The gun showed excellent performance on the battlefield, earning respect for its range and impressive destructive ability.

Thanks to its six-cylinder Maybach engine, the Pz.I light tank - mass produced since July 1943 - was fast and manoeuvrable, while its turret-mounted double machine guns proved to be an excellent tool against enemy infantry. However, light armor and the lack of a gun rendered the Pz.I useless in tank battles.

The production of Wehrmacht's last light tank began in 1942. The Lynx, with its 20mm autogun and light armor, did not pose a serious threat to enemy tanks, yet its six-gear transmission allowed it to reach high speeds. Thanks to this advantage, it was ideally suited for recon missions, which earned it appropriate respect.

In order to clear minefields, German engineers have developed a special mine roller. When mounted upon the chassis of a Pz.Kpfw.III tank, it allowed the vehicle to drive through minefields unharmed. The resulting corridors were then used by infantry and ordinary tanks. It was armed with only a machine-gun.

In production since September 1940, the Pz.IV Ausf.E received 30mm armor plates, additionally reinforced by a 30mm shield. However, these modifications did not produce the desired effect, and the Pz.IV's short-barrelled gun was still unable to penetrate the armor of Soviet KV and T-34 tanks, which, in contrast, were defeating these poorly protected vehicles with ease. Nevertheless, the Pz.IV Ausf.E continued to be effective as a means of support infantry.

In April 1943 another modification of the most popular German tank came to the fore. This machine differed from its predecessors due to its enhanced armor and improved armament. Its armor was 80mm thick while the mounted screens on its sides ensured reliable protection from high-explosion rounds. The new long-barrelled Kwk40 L/48 boasted excellent combat performance and was successfully used to fight medium enemy tanks.

For a long time this long-barrelled 17-pound gun was considered the best in its class. It was adopted by the British Army at the same time as the enemy's newest heavy tanks arrived in North Africa. For this reason, mass production of the gun started as quickly as possible. High armor-piercing performance and excellent ballistic qualities enabled the QF 17 to destroy almost any German vehicle from a long range. However, the gun's excessive weight greatly hindered its transportation.

The British 2-pounder developed in 1936 was considered one of the best guns in its class. During the early years of the war, the QF2 was successfully used to fight enemy APCs, light and medium tanks. The arrival of more heavily-protected Panzers quickly reduced its efficiency however.

One of the most successful models of German motorcycles entered mass production in 1934. Fast and armed with an MG-34 machine-gun (mounted on a sidecar), the R-12 became very popular among Wehrmacht motorized troops.

Production of these 4 x 4 light armored vehicles started in 1936. Thanks to its good ride performance this vehicle became very popular among German troops and was widely used in the initial battles of World War Two. An automatic gun installed on its small rotating turret, coupled with a 20mm machine gun, effectively struck at enemy personnel and light armored equipment. However, the insufficient protection of the SdKfz 222 was the reason it was downgraded to reconnaissance and support equipment.

The SdKfz 251 half-track armored vehicle entered service with the Wehrmacht in the summer of 1939. It was widely used as a means of troop transport along the Soviet-German front, but because of its open top, the crew wasn't sufficiently protected. Apart from seats, the infantry compartment contained mounts for several machine guns. The Hanomag engine allowed this 9-tonne vehicle to achieve high speeds, while sloping armor plates provided some protection to the transported infantry.

Smoke trails behind a Nebelwerfer's rocket volley exposed its position and made it very vulnerable to counter-attacks, so it was decided to mount this weapon on a mobile platform. The first versions of the Sdkzf.4 with a mounted rocket launcher entered service with the Wehrmacht in early 1944. Bullet-proof armor and fair manoeuvrability increased the vehicle's overall resilience while a volley of ten 150mm rockets was capable of inflicting devastating damage on the enemy.

Serial production of these rather basic but effective mobile anti-aircraft systems began in 1940.  The machine presented a standard German half-track armored vehicle with a combined 4-barrelled Flakvierling 38 anti-aircraft gun mounted on the body. This 20mm automatic gun could fire up to 1,800 shots per minute, successfully hitting low-flying enemy aircraft, infantry or light armored equipment. At the same time poor cockpit protection and the resulting vulnerability of the gun crew lead to heavy losses in open combat.

The Stug assault gun, mounted on the PzKpfw IV chassis, entered production in December 1943 and was mainly used as a means of defence from enemy counter-attacks. Its low profile and sturdy, sloping frontal armor helped increase the overall resilience, which, combined with the turret-mounted 75mm gun, allowed the tank to accomplish combat objectives with maximum efficiency. Anti-HEAT armor plates were frequently mounted on the sides to further improve its defensive capabilities.

Mass-production of assault howitzers mounted on a StuG III self-propelled gun chassis and using its cockpit began in March 1943. The Sturmhaubitze 42 first saw combat at the Kursk Bulge and later successfully served in Africa and Western Europe. A 105mm round fired from its gun was quite efficient in destroying the enemy's light field fortifications and bunkers, making this machine indispensable for storming fortified areas. These well armored self-propelled howitzers entered service with assault gun battalions as direct support to infantry and tanks on the battlefield.

The German Army's operations on the eastern front proved that Germany desperately needed well protected, self-propelled assault guns capable of quickly destroying the fortifications and long-term defences of the Red Army. The chassis of the Pz.IVe heavy tank met all of these requirements, so the new machines inherited it with almost no changes. Instead of a turret, a fixed cockpit made of strategically positioned thick armor plates was installed housing a modified 380mm Raketenwerfer 61 naval rocket launcher. In August 1944 the first prototype of the Sturmtiger was trialled during the Warsaw Uprising. The self-propelled gun proved itself an excellent weapon for the purposes of destroying fortifications and neutralising enemy firing posts. However its heavy armor negatively influenced its ride characteristics.

This Soviet self-propelled gun was developed in record-breaking time; less than a month passed between the start of the design work and its adoption by the Red Army. A high calibre, high-explosion round had a big damaging and destructive effect. This enabled the SU-122 to fight not only field fortifications but also long-term enemy fortified structures. The chassis of the T-34 medium tank ensured excellent mobility of the machine which, together with a low profile and reasonably good armor, had a positive impact on its ability to survive. Although such self-propelled guns normally moved in the rear echelon of advancing troops, the absence of a machine gun to fight enemy infantry was its big drawback.

The SU-76 entered mass production during the autumn of 1942. Chassis from the light T-70 tank provided it with great speed and manoeuvrability, while the turret-mounted ZIS-3 field gun showed excellent performance in battle. Its one significant disadvantage was the incomplete and weak armor. In spite of that, the SU-76 was successful in defeating light and medium enemy tanks.

Created in 1943, the SU-85 self-propelled artillery piece was designed to fight against the then-appearing Tiger and Panther tanks. The upgraded 85mm D-5S anti-aircraft gun was mounted atop the T34's chassis, combining the latter's great speed and manoeuvrability with formidable firepower. The SU-85 was largely used to provide fire support to T-34s and advancing infantry.

Soviet light tank with a low-velocity, low calibre main armament. 3 man crew.   A two-turreted Vickers-E tank entered service with the Red Army on February 13th, 1931. It was designated T-26, and since 1939 it was produced as a single-turret vehicle armed with a 45mm gun and sloped hull armor plates. By the beginning of war the tank had already become obsolete, but some were still used for recon missions and infantry support.

Soviet mass-produced T34 tank mark 1, upgunned to match and surpass any armored fighting vehicle on the battlefield at the time of it's deployment. Fast, agile and nible and capable of unprecedented speeds, best used as a breath-through vehicle to carve into enemy defensive lines.   This version had a long-barrelled anti-tank gun, able to compete with the outstanding German KwK40 in terms of armor penetration and ballistic characteristics. The armor and chassis remained the same: armor plates sloped at 30 degrees, providing the relatively thin hull with good resistance to shelling, while the 500hp diesel engine guaranteed excellent speed and manoeuvrability.

Soviet mass-produced T34 tank mark 2, upgunned and up-armored with the added benefit of radio and larger turret housing.   The 1943 version differs from its predecessor in terms of improved armor and a roomier, six-sided turret, which allowed the designers to equip the tank with an upgraded 76mm F34 gun and supply it with more ordnance. These changes did not affect the already outstanding advantages of the most prominent Soviet medium tank - the speed and manoeuvrability of T34s remained the same.

Soviet mass-produced T34 tank mark 3, the final iteration of the T34 series, this battle-honed variant has the best of offensive innovations sporting a highly powerful main cannon and turret super-structure. This vehicle deserves no better place than to be at the front of an army leading the attack.   This modification entered service with the Red Army on January 23rd, 1944. In order to mount a powerful 85mm anti-tank gun some changes had to be introduced into its turret design: it became larger and more heavily protected. Side and rear armor was also enhanced, which, in combination with its sharp slope angle, significantly increased the shell resistance of the hull. As a result the T-34's weight increased to 32 tonnes and the tank became a bit slower, yet its combat efficiency has significantly risen.

Soviet mine clearer, using the mass-produced T34 chassis as its base. Armed with 1 machinegun. 3 crew.   A T34 modification, designed specifically to deal with minefields, introduced the PT-3 mine trawl, which consisted basically of two rollers installed on a forward platform. Considered unnecessary, the tank's gun turret was often removed, leaving the vehicle with just a machine gun.

The most-produced Soviet light tank of World War 2 was commissioned by the Red Army in January 1942. It differed from its predecessors in its improved armor, lower profile and higher manoeuvrability. A quiet engine provided the machine with excellent speed and allowed it to stealthily access the enemy rear where the T70 could attack the most vulnerable enemy areas with its 45mm gun. At the same time poor protection from rounds of all calibres made this tank a perfect target for enemy guns which is why it was used only for reconnaissance and direct infantry support.

The Wirbelwind self-propelled anti-aircraft gun, based on the Pz.IV chassis, was developed in 1944. Its armor was identical to that of the tank's, while the turret was removed and replaced with an open-top, nine-sided housing with a quadruple 20mm Flak 38 gun. The Wirbelwind performed well against low-flying airborne targets, and in times of need could be used to destroy enemy infantry.

In a short period of time three US companies: Willys, Ford and Bantam developed a reliable and efficient off-roader for military needs. Its production began in 1941. It quickly proved its worth on the battlefield - the excellent speed and possibility to mount large-calibre machine guns made Willys one of the finest army vehicles of WWII.

In 1941 about a hundred Komsomolet armored tractors were upgraded and converted into open-type, self-propelled vehicles by mounting long-barrelled 57mm guns on them. The new machines were given the name ZiS-30 and had entered the field by the end of September. The anti-tank guns proved excellent in fighting light and medium enemy equipment but insufficient protection of the cockpit and the high vulnerability of the crew lead to heavy losses among these SPGs in their very first outings.

Soviet high powered anti-tank field gun, mark 2, 57mm calibre with additional APC type shot.   The ZIS-2 anti-tank gun entered mass production on June 1, 1941, but its production was soon halted and had not been resumed until first German Tiger and Panther tanks appeared on the field of battle. Due to a specially designed breech-block, this long-barrelled artillery piece demonstrated high rate of fire, while also being lightweight and compact. Firing 57mm armor-piercing rounds, it could penetrate even heavy German tanks. Despite all these advantages, its high-explosive rounds were much underpowered, hampering the ZIS's usage against enemy personnel or fortifications.

Soviet highly capable anti-tank field gun, 76mm calibre with additional APC type shot.   ZIS-3 is the world's first conveyor-assembled artillery piece. It was highly praised by the artillery specialists and on February 12, 1942 entered service with the Red Army. Firing armor-piercing rounds, it was able to penetrate 70mm of armor at medium range, while its high-explosive shells demonstrated high stopping power and a great damage radius.

Soviet multi-purpose truck able to carry procurements, troops or tow heavy weaponry.   The 3-tonne Soviet ZIS-5 truck entered mass production in the early 1930s. Easy to maintain, it achieved relatively high speeds and was used during the war for transporting troops, cargo and towing artillery.

Inside this truck you will find tools for repairing equipment, materials for building obstacles and defences and anti-personnel and anti-tank mines. Obstacles are usually built in front of occupied positions or sometimes on the flanks and in the gaps between them. Defences are made of sandbags and serve to strengthen the positions of friendly infantry.   The Soviet 3-ton ZIS-5 truck was mass produced during the 1930s. Despite being undemanding, this truck could reach fairly high speeds and, during the war, was used to transport troops, cargo and artillery. It also served as an ambulance and petrol tanker.

Inside this truck you will find a repair kit, small arms and light artillery ammo, grenades, mines and other ammunition.   The Soviet 3-ton ZIS-5 truck was mass-produced during the 1930s. Despite its simplicity, it could reach fairly high speeds and, during the war, was used to transport troops, cargo and artillery. It also served as an ambulance and petrol tanker.

Soviet ground-level self-propelled anti-vehicle and anti-infantry weapons platform. Utilisng the Su76 chasis, armed with a 37mm quick-firing cannon.  A self-propelled anti-aircraft gun based on the SU-76 chassis. It entered service with the Red Army in 1945. Its 37mm AA-gun could be used not only against enemy aircraft, but also against light and even medium tanks. Its weak armor was well compensated by good speed and manoeuvrability.

The first thing you need to know as infantrymen, is to ALWAYS seek cover. In the open, you are vulnerable. Cover improves your survivability and your aim. Now, take cover behind the sandbags.
We seem to be clear... MG team 1, stay here. Everyone else, forward, take positions on the stone wall. Los gehts!
The Bolsheviks will be coming down that road any minute now. We will ambush them. Soldaten, get ready!
Alright, I can see the Ivans! Hold your fire until they're in front of us.
Very good. You have achieved your first kills. The more kills you achieve, the higher your veterancy. You will improve your shooting and survival skills.
Our neighboring squad has found a pocket of resistance up ahead. There is an MG pinning our boys down. We are behind them! I need you to get close and throw a grenade on that MG nest.
Well done, men! Finish these Ivans off!
Look at that, the Ivans have unwillingly brought us a truck! Go and look if it has any weaponry we can loot!
Damn it! There's a soviet tank ambushing us from the other side of the farm! Get behind it and destroy it with the AT grenades that you have acquired.

Fortunately, we are prepared for this. Take command of the AT rifleman, and turn that armored car into Swiss cheese!
Well done, men! You have completed my instructions to the letter.
Welcome to boot camp, Soldier. In this tutorial, you will learn how to control infantry, the most common and important type of unit on the battlefield.
During a cutscene, you cannot control your units. Some cutscenes, like this one, can be skipped. To do so, press the "continue" button on the top-right corner.

To move your soldier, select him and right-click on the destination. A double click will make him sprint until his stamina runs out. If you move your cursor close to objects, it will prompt the soldier to take cover, previewing a silhouette. Now, make your soldier take cover with the rest of the men.
Well done. You should always move your troops from one cover to the next.

Approach the MG nest carefully from behind. Move from one bush or cover to the next. A prone soldier will be harder to spot. When the MG nest is taken out, the rest of the squad will assist you in taking out the remaining Soviets.

Select your soldier, and press 'X' or click on the 'examine' icon. When you hover over the vehicle, the cursor will change to an eye. Transfer any AT grenades from the inventory of the truck to your soldier's inventory.
Infantry can move in any terrain, but vehicles, especially wheeled vehicles, must use roads to travel at maximum speed, which makes them easy to ambush.

Buildings and other objects block the line of sight of units. You can see the enemy tank because other friendly units are actively fighting it. But no enemy unit is currently able to see your soldier. Because of this, you can easily flank the enemy tank without being detected.
You must be aware of your mission objectives. You can always open your mission tasks with the hotkey "O".

Quite often, you will need to get rid of remaining enemies to proceed with the next stages of a mission. Keep an eye out for enemies who may be concealed in the "fog of war", for example, hiding in trenches.

Welcome to boot camp, Soldier.  In this tutorial, you will learn how to control infantry, the most common and important type of unit in the battlefield.                                          Good luck!
Take cover behind the stone wall.
Take out the MG nest with a grenade.

Welcome to the front line! This will be your first tank combat experience, so pay attention for your own survival.
Now, Soldiers. We don't have much time. Move the tank to a suitable firing position.
Enemy vehicles down the road! Wipe them out!
Excellent job! Now you must turn your attention to the broken track. We must keep our vehicles operational at all times!
Ah! The supply truck has arrived! Just in time to replenish the shells you just used up!
Very well. Now, move forward and take control of the enemy checkpoint ahead!
Enemy tank! A heavily armored one!
Good shot! That's how it's done!

Alright, commander! You seem to have gotten the hang of it. Now, go forward, and eliminate the last enemy position. Choose your targets wisely, and feel free to return to the supply truck for resupply.
The Bolsheviks left us some fuel trucks! What a lovely surprise. No doubt, you should consider refueling after this arduous trip. Go see to it.
Well done! You have acquired all the basic skills to fight in armored vehicles. I'm sure you will become a highly skilled tank commander!
Behold, the Panzer IV Ausf. F1. This is the best our Wehrmacht has to offer. A multi-role tank, capable of supporting our infantry and dealing with enemy armor.
Now, move the tank to position behind the sandbags.

Your tank is immobilised, because the track was broken. We will deal with it later. The first order of business is eliminating the enemy threat. Engage enemy tanks with AP shells. The tank will automatically load the correct shell type for its target, but you can control ammo selection manually in third person or direct control.

Your tank is equipped with 5 repair kits. Each repair kit will repair one vehicle component, then it is consumed. To begin the repair, select the tank and click on the "repair" button. A crew will automatically disembark and repair the tank's damaged components in order of priority. You can also manually disembark a crew member, select the repair button, and click on the tank.

Your tank automatically prioritized firing at the enemy tanks first, then the armored car. When armored threats are eliminated, tanks will automatically switch to high-exposive shells to engage infantry.

Tank crew, artillerymen, and engineers can repair vehicles much faster than ordinary soldiers. Tank crew also have greater skill and accuracy with the tank's main cannon. Always try to replace any lost crew with properly trained tankmen.
Resupply your tank by bringing it within the resupply radius of the supply vehicle.

Enemy infantry are most easily dealt with using High Explosive (HE) shells and with the tank's secondary armament. However, it may be inconvenient if enemy armor arrives and your tank has to spend valuable time switching to AP shells to engage it. For this reason, there is a button to "lock" the vehicle to only use the currently selected shell type and to not switch to other shells on its own.
You will have to use HEAT shells to penetrate the thicker, sloped armor of the enemy T-34 tank.
To refuel your tank, bring it within the refuel radius of the fuel trucks.

Due to the complexity of armored combat, a well-managed tank can make all the difference in the battlefield.                                          Good luck!
Move the tank into a defensive position.
Storm and capture the enemy checkpoint, focusing on enemy infantry with HE shells.

What is this?! It's a heavy Soviet tank, a KV-1! Take it out immediately using APCR rounds!

An exceptional kill! Now, kill the remaining enemy soldiers!

Airstrikes and artillery strikes are now available to be called in.
Your orders are to attack the enemy with both air and artillery strikes!
Intelligence suggests Russians have a heavy tank at their HQ. An airstrike would be most effective to deal with that problem!
Skip the preparation phase when you’re ready!
Mission Accomplished!  Click on 'continue' to keep playing this mission or click on 'next' to proceed directly into the next mission.

Welcome to support weaponry training, Soldier.  In this tutorial, you will learn the basics of reinforcements. This includes calling in additional standard units and requesting support assets such as artillery and air strikes.                                        Good luck!
Call in the Rifle Squad and move them into the trenches!
Call in a MG 34, a 8cm Mortar and a 2cm Flak. Place them on the frontline (green outline) to defend our HQ!
Carefully advance towards - and shoot a flare at - the enemy outpost!
Call off-map Airstrike on enemy targets!
Call off-map Artillery on enemy targets!
Do not blow things up in the fuel area!
A man has been killed! Unacceptable!
Grenades must not explode in the area of the shooting range.

There are 2 ways you can refuel a vehicle: automatically, by driving a refueling supply truck close to it, or manually, with fuel cans. To use fuel cans, collect them into your soldier's inventory, and while holding them, clicking on a fuel source like fuel trucks and big barrels to fill the empty can with fuel. When the can is full, you can "pour out" the fuel contents into the empty vehicle.

Select your soldier, and move him around with your mouse clicks. You can examine boxes by clicking on them to transfer the items between the box's and soldier's inventories. Grab a helmet, rifle, and ammo from the different boxes.

You can throw grenades to eliminate targets behind cover. For the most effective use of grenades, you can 'cook' them in direct control mode (select a single soldier and press the direct control button on the bottom left of the interface or press the hotkey 'E' by default). Direct control allows you to micro-control one unit with WASD movement and mouse aiming/shooting.

You can highlight objects that can be collected by your units - like the weapons on the table - by clicking on the 'highlight items' button on the bottom right corner of the interface 'cubed shape button' or by holding the hotkey 'C' by default

You can always open the Mission Objectives menu using the button on the bottom right of the interface or by clicking 'O' by default. You can click on each mission objective to show where it takes place on the map. Secondary mission objectives are not essential for the completion of the mission.

You will need to manually shoot the targets in direct control. Press "E" by default to switch to direct control with the selected unit. Press "T" by default to toggle "Classic" and "Third Person" modes. Note that the longer you aim at a target, the more accurate your shot will be.
You now have control of three more soldiers.

Different components of vehicles can be damaged on the battlefield (tracks, engine, gun, turret, body, etc.). You will need repair kits to repair these components. You can find them in most vehicle's inventory. Repair kits are a single-use item. If multiple components are broken, you will need a repair kit for each component. Take a repair kit from the vehicle into your soldier's inventory, then with the soldier selected, press the repair button in the bottom right corner of the interface (Wrench icon). Lastly, click on the vehicle to order your soldier to repair it.

Get to cover behind the sandbags and get ready to fire. Select your soldiers, and hover the cursor close to the sandbag. A silhouette previews the position of your soldiers behind cover. Utilize cover as much as possible to increase the survivability and accuracy of your soldiers.
Do not leave the hideout area before completing the task. If you leave the hideout, new targets will not appear.
You can place different weapons on the tripod. Start off by collecting an MG-34 machine gun from the box and put it in the tripod's inventory. You can examine vehicles' inventory by pressing "X".

Now you have to mount the machinegun. To do so, crew the tripod and open the tripod’s inventory by selecting it and hitting the hotkey 'I' by default. Double click on the machinegun in the inventory to mount it. Now shoot all the targets in the firing range. You will notice mounted weapons are more accurate and have less recoil.
Good luck, Soldiers. Make the fatherland proud!
That is the fuel station. Our vehicles need fuel to keep on running. You should familiarize yourself with the refueling process.
That truck must stay within the gasoline station grounds.
Good work, Soldiers. Now head over to the grenade area. Use the hand grenades to blow up some of the fuel barrels.
The Karabiner 98-K is the standard infantry weapon. A precise bolt action rifle, ideal for engaging the enemy at medium and long ranges.

This is the MG and Mortar range. Infantry support weapons are essential, and you should train using them. You need to man these vehicles with at least two operators to move them, and they are very effective when placed in strategic positions.

This is the Cannon range. Here we will show you how to engage enemy armored targets with a variety of projectiles. Crew the 3.7cm PaK anti-tank gun with your soldiers to begin the ballistics briefing!

The 3.7cm PaK Light Anti-Tank Gun fires various types of ammunition. To penetrate and destroy armored targets, use Armor Piercing (AP) and Armor Piercing Composite Rigid (APCR) rounds. To penetrate the thicker plates in front of you, use APCR. Against angled armor APCR it will ricochet off instead of penetrating. AP shells are more effective in this case.

For wooden or other soft targets, High Explosive (HE) shells are best. These shells detonate on impact and cause a lot of damage to non-armored objects, unlike AP shells that would pass through and cause little damage.

The high-velocity APCR shells are lightweight and penetrate more than AP shells at close ranges but they lose their kinetic energy quickly at longer ranges. It is better to use AP shells to engage distant targets.

Now you have acquired basic weapons training. You may look around the facilities and explore all the testing grounds which Kummersdorf has to offer. You will find the latest military equipment on various testing grounds.
Once you consider yourself ready for posting, board the trucks at the dispersal area. You will be delivered to your regiments.
Now you must learn your weapon and put your aim to the test. Head to the western shooting range!
Get ready to shoot at the targets! Take cover behind the sandbags!

Welcome to the intensive training camp for special forces soldiers. In front of you is a combined obstacle course for different types of battles, which will help you get acquainted with the weapon in the closest possible conditions.
When you're ready to take the course, go to the entrance.
It is better to use a machine gun to pass the first stage. The most effective medium to long-range weapon against superior opponents.
Once you're ready to climb over the fence, the obstacle course timer will begin. Take a position at the indicated point and hit all targets that rise.
Well done! Not bad at all. Now, move on to the next stage.
For combat in confined spaces, a submachine gun is best suited. Also, use grenades to quickly and safely clean the rooms.
Hit all targets to complete this stage!
Remember, heavy anti-tank grenades can be used to blow up obstacles in your path.
You can accurately throw grenades in direct control mode. Narrow windows and cracks are not a hindrance for you. Throw grenades inside these two fortifications and damage the barrels.
You are a very capable soldier, just what the Reich needs. Let's proceed to the final stage.
Get on the motorcycle. Hook up the cannon and move to the final point. In strategic mode, you can set the path for the unit if you hold down the "Shift" and give orders with the left mouse button.
You're damn good. In the upcoming battles, Germany can rely on you.
Complete amateurs are being hired now. You are a disgrace to Germany.
Soldiers! Welcome to the Kummersdorf training camp.
We expect nothing but the very best from all of you.
We are on the brink of war! Here you will undergo basic combat training to defend the fatherland! First off, grab a helmet, grab your weapon and grab some ammunition.
That tank must stay within the test-drive grounds.
Shoot at the targets, soldiers! Steady your aim for as long as possible to get the most accurate shots.

The Wehrmacht counts with the finest weaponry available to any infantryman. A variety of automatic and precision weapons are available on the tables. Some are more effective for short-range fights and others favor long-distance engagements. Use your preferred armament against the next set of targets!
Behold the latest design of our armed forces! The Panzer III. With this kind of armor, nobody can stop us. Feel free to board this tank and take it for a test drive.
In front of you is an obstacle course. Move to the highlighted points and destroy targets as quickly as possible!
For effective control of the tank, switch to direct control mode using the "E" key.

Remember to choose the right weapon type. Use machine guns to destroy the infantry. In direct control mode, switch quickly to specific weapons using the keys 1-4 or right mouse click to cycle through all the weapons.
Great job! I see this tank will become your favorite in battle.
You disappoint me. You better not mess with the tank troops.

Damn it! Aaahhh! .... Hey, you! Can you lend me a hand here? I've injured my hand but I still have to get this tank up and running for this evening's exercises. If you can, get some repair tools and fix it!
Thank you very much, soldier. I see you have some useful skills!
Just 2 weeks after this, the second world war started. The Gates of Hell were opened.
Make sure you're ready to go to war. You will not survive without the right skills! Keep going, you will learn.
In this mission, you can learn the basics of gameplay.
Equip your soldier with a helmet, a rifle and ammo (at least 20 rifle rounds).
Eliminate all the targets at the shooting range.
Blow up all the barrels with grenades.
Board the vehicle to conclude the military camp training.
Go to the armored vehicle test area for vehicle test driving.
Go to the repair workshop for mechanic training.
Go to the AT gun shooting range for armored combat training.
Go to the supply station for refuel training.
Attend the MG and mortar shooting range training.
Go to the advanced training course for special forces.
Time to overcome the obstacle course:
Time to complete the special training course:
Your medic was not fast enough and the soldier bled to death.
There you go! The first mine popped up. I'm sure there's more!
Alright, I think that's all of them.

When the terrain will not give you cover, you should dig your own entrenchments. Soldiers require a foxhole shovel to dig. There is a "fortifications" submenu on the bottom right where you can choose what to build. Engineers can erect a wider range of items.

Medics are one of the most valuable assets on the battlefield. They are the only ones who can treat bleeding soldiers. While having a medic selected, hover over an injured soldier and you will be prompted to treat him. Bear in mind, bleeding soldiers will die if left unattended for too long...

You must use a mine detector to locate mines. To do so, grab it from the truck's inventory. Once in your soldiers' inventory, you will be able to sweep a specific location using the 'mine detection' button inside the 'item options' submenu on the bottom right.
Repair kits are inside each vehicle. If you run out of repair kits, you will have to scavenge for them.

There is ammunition dispersed among crates. To refuel, you need to bring in a fuel truck close to the vehicle or alternatively scavenge for fuel using a jerrycan which can be found inside the vehicle.

To mine an area, click the "AT Mine" or "AP Mine" icons in the "Items" menu. Point to the area by left-clicking anywhere on the map. Holding shift and point will queue planting mines in various locations. Holding the left-click and dragging the cursor allows placing a number of mines in a line. Your soldier will start mining from his location in the direction of the click. It takes a soldier a few moments to plant each mine, AT-mines take longer to plant for example.
Here they come! Hold your ground!
We're engaged! Get down, everybody! Some Soviet border patrol must have heard us!
We will provide suppressive fire! MEDIC! Take care of that man!
They know we're here, and more patrols must be on their way. We will fend off any counter-attack! Dig foxholes, move it! If you need more shovels, there's more in the truck.
Area cleared! Excellent job. You are making the fatherland proud!
It wasn't hard to make them talk. Apparently, Ivan has yet another platoon in the northern part of the village. Our orders are to take them out.
Wait a moment... That tank looks operational. We should attempt to repair and service it. It will make our job much easier!
The truck is done. We will continue on foot and start by demining this road.
You! Grab a mine detector from the truck and sweep the road ahead!
This thing has no ammo, no fuel! What a bloody disaster. You'll need to stock her up!

I need you to take your half of the squad and flank the village from the north. Get those bastards from the side and grenade them out of their festering stinkholes. We will keep them spotted and have their guns pointed this way!
Get to cover! We're being fired upon from the village!

Damn it! We were supposed to secure this area without much opposition! The invasion has not taken these communists by surprise! They seem to have a whole detachment in that village. They've fortified their position with MGs.
Try your hand at commanding troops and vehicles in your baptism of fire.
Hold your position against the counterattack.
Dig at least 2 foxholes and prepare to repel any counterattacks.
Flank the village, take out all the MGs and neutralize the perimeter.
Drive the enemy out of the entire settlement.
Mine the road in preparation for the enemy convoy.
Plant at least 10 AP mines in this area!
Plant at least 10 AT mines in this area!
A Russian convoy will soon be traveling along the eastern road from the north. Mine the road across the bridge!
Soldiers, grab both antipersonnel and anti-tank mines from the truck. Plant each at the marked locations!
You planted %1%/10 AP mines in the ordered area.
You planted %1%/10 AT mines in the ordered area.
Here are your reinforcements. Better late than never...
A convoy is approaching! Stay down and hide, allow them to drive into the minefield before attacking!
Well done soldier. You survived your first battle. Looks like we will be able to count on you.
Make sure you follow orders and make sure you do it quickly. You don't want to end up in a Strafbatalion!
Click on the area to bombard.
%1% out of 5 dummy guns built. You need to take 2 cords of wood to each of the emplacement locations. Dummy guns will attract enemy artillery fire.
Select the artillery barrage and click on the designated firing area. Obtain points by kills.
Enemy artillery is about to fire on the crosshair location.
Comrades, welcome, great timing. We're seriously down on manpower here. Wait... Is this all of you?!!
Well... we're up shit creek without a paddle! We know the fascists want to smash through here to get to Moscow. We must do everything we can to stop them!
They're attacking! Get our artillery ready to kill them! Hold the line!!
I think that plane was a spotter! Enemy artillery will attempt to destroy our AT guns!
That plane is scouting for our AT guns! Enemy artillery will shoot at whatever he observed!
The High Command has mobilized our reserves, including a new prototype tank. Comrade, no German vehicle will survive a shot from this monster. Send the Fascist vermin back to hell where they belong!
The Fascists have entered the village! Take them out immediately, or we will be done for!
You had been ordered to not let the Germans inside the village! There is no room for cowards and traitors in our Red Army!
Fetch these coordinates! Give them hell!
Fire on these coordinates! I want to hear them scream!
We should lay mines. We must man the AT guns. Let's go!
The Germans use spotters to find targets for their artillery and their planes. We've collected some timber to build dummy guns. If you care for your men - you better distract their artillery!
Artillery is down! We'll have to do without the big guns!

Operation Typhoon started with great prospects for the Germans, but soon the tenacious Soviet resistance made it harder and harder for the Germans to make further gains. The harsh winter conditions, the constant attrition of combat and the stubbornness of the Soviet defenses slowed the relentless Blitzkrieg to a standstill. With fresh reserves from the east, the Stavka would order a counterattack. The road to Berlin was to begin. The outcome of the Great Patriotic War was now inevitable.   For the successful defense of the station of Dubosekovo, a number of monuments were built in honor of Panfilov’s 28 men who were collectively declared heroes of the Soviet Union. In reality, the story turned out to be fabricated. There were many more men in the fight, and the losses for the 8th  Guards Rifle Division were much greater. Comrade General Panfilov died two days later, on November 18th.

Because you were unable to stop the attack, the Germans march on unopposed and will most likely surround Moscow very soon. Our reinforcements from the east will not make it in time to hold Moscow. This will be a huge blow to morale!
Volokolamsk road. Less than 100 km away from Moscow.
The German forces launch an attack on Volokolamsk during “Operation Typhoon”, in order to circumvent the northern part of the Moscow defense line.
Do not let the enemy reach Dubosekovo!
Build dummy guns to bait the enemy artillery fire.
The Germans have entered the village! Clear it out and don't let them enter again!

Tikhvin was as far east as ‘Army Group North’ would ever get. The Soviet counter-attack of December 41 pushed the Germans out almost exactly one month after it had been lost. Once re-taken, the Soviets never lost control of the Tikhvin railway hub again and Leningrad would not fall, despite the fact that the siege lasted almost 900 days.

Because you lost the battle, the people of Leningrad will receive even smaller rations than they already have until now. The situation has just become critical! There is no way of saying how many people will pay with their lives for this failure.
Compromise the garrison! %1% Out of a minimum of 4 targets accomplished.
Nighttime reduces the units' vision but vehicles and loud gunshots will be heard over a distance. Try to be stealthy.
Look for something to contaminate the fuel tank. Get a soldier to bring the item close to the hatch.
To contaminate the enemy kitchen, take a soldier with a repair kit in his hands and bring it to the kitchen area. Engine lubricants are not particularly edible.
To take out the German howitzers silently, bring a soldier close enough to the gun barrel and he will sabotage the gun.
There are several paths leading to the second aerosled. Scouting will be needed to determine the best one.
Try to remain stealthy. Do not get too close to sleeping Germans or raise suspicion. You should use the silenced Nagant pistol to take out enemies quietly.
A high-ranking officer is performing an inspection. He may carry documents. You must wait for the right time to ambush him.
The target may be eliminated silently. Come closer for instructions.
There is a fuel supply area which we should sabotage. Quietly, if possible... I have some ideas.
Full throttle! He's right behind us!
Go through the shrubs! He won't know where we went!
We have to regroup with the other aerosled! .... the radio caught a bullet, we can't communicate ... we will have to find them using another way!
We have the documents! Let me see...
A Panzer got on our tail and we had to evade it using a different route, but our radio was broken... what's the status?
Abort? No! We must take action now while they are resting. First, we must find out where their depots and supplies are, and destroy them.
I can translate German... sounds like a cunning plan... Let's go.
Hmm. It seems we laid our hands on the complete plan of the defense sectors and units located here, plus the scheduled arrival of new logistic columns. This is pure gold, comrades.
We will wreak all sorts of havoc while we can! We could potentially visit.... let's see... An artillery position! The barracks! The fuel depot...

Apparently, judging by the distance between German units, they rely on a powerful radio vehicle for communication. If we can take that out, the Germans here will be isolated. Look for antennas to find it...
Don't let us get spotted or noticed by enemy officers! Make sure to shoot them before engaging in combat. They will likely call for reinforcements!
That officer over there is still safe and sound! I bet he's calling for reinforcements as we speak. Brace yourselves!
See that guy with the peaked cap? He's an officer! You should have taken him out by now! I bet he is calling in reinforcements.
Bloody hell, this place stinks of petrol. The fuel must have an open valve somewhere. Hmmm... We could put some chemicals into the fuel to stall their engines...

I'm sure we don't want to interrupt their sleep... What a great occasion. Why don't we introduce a new ingredient onto the kitchen ovens? Erm... go fetch a repair kit. I'm sure there are some delicious lubricants and anti-freezing fluids in there.

Aha, there's the artillery. I suspect if we blow them up, the noise will alert the fascists. How about we take out the guards silently... and then we put some pebbles in the gun barrels? Next time they fire... they will have some surprise fireworks!
Comrades, in a few minutes a fuel convoy is scheduled to arrive. We should take it out!
A logistics column is scheduled to arrive in a few minutes. The Manifest: Howitzer ammunition. I don't think we should let the fascist dogs have any of that!
Oh yes. Guten appetit, you swine!
Alright, comrades. That's enough. Time to get the hell out!
Hah! They won't know what hit 'em.
Excellent. They can't call for reinforcements now. But this is no license to go out there with guns blazing! They still outnumber us and we should try and act quietly!
The officer by the roadblock might be calling in reinforcements, kill him right now!
I bet that officer just called for reinforcements!
That officer by the sandbags will have called in reinforcements by now!
Officer spotted! Don't let him detect you!
Officer! Don't get into a fight without killing him first, or else he might call for reinforcements.
Damn! We woke them up! I guess the only way to sabotage this place now is to kill everybody.
There is an artillery battery which we must take care of. I got an idea for taking them out silently when we get there.
The Fascists have some designated barracks. I'm sure we could stealthily deal with them while they sleep.
There is a fuel supply area which we should sabotage. Quietly, if possible... I have some ideas.
Comrades! Thanks for helping us! Let us help you on your mission!
Comrade Commissar! We thought you were dead! We have been unable to contact you since we approached Tikhvin!
Not good Sir... It's full of Germans building defenses. It's suicidal to attack the enemy garrison. Should we abort?
How shall we proceed, comrade Commissar?
We're getting away! The German's tracks are sinking into the snow!
Comrade Commissar, the road is blocked. This way leads to the German rear... We're lost!
Comrade Commissar, the Germans always write everything down. We could look out for a high-ranking officer and take his documents.
Comrade Commissar, how will we manage to prevent the Germans from calling in reinforcements?
I can't see movement at those barracks, they must be asleep. Hmm, smells sweet. They must be preparing breakfast already.
Something's going on over by the lamp post. What the hell?!
Shit! Those tanks over there are being manned! Stop making noise!
I see an officer! Watch out!
That is an officer! Don't let him see you...
Army Group North dashes towards the key city of Leningrad. Tikhvin is taken.  The Red Army orders a counteroffensive for the next day. In preparation, the lines are infiltrated.
Establish contact with the other aerosled.
Medic! - Commissar is wounded and requires first aid!
Revive Commissar before he bleeds to death!
The Commissar must obtain the German documents. He can read German.
Ambush and destroy the ammo convoy.
Take out the radio vehicle to disable enemy communications.
What is that in front of us?
Flank the enemy at once, otherwise, our comrades will be obliterated.
We will mourn them later. Keep going, otherwise, we will be dead too!
Comrades, you are now under my command.
We must protect our trucks along the length of the entire road!
Prepare defensive positions, dig trenches and foxholes, and mine the approaches to the road! You can find ammunition and mines in the trucks.
We were attacked by enemy recon units.
The Germans broke through to the road, regain the initiative and drive them out!
Secure the positions near the road! Drive the Germans away!
We need to send scouts up ahead. Ivanov, move forward and report German movement.
They are coming back in full strength. Hold positions!
We must use this time to strengthen the defenses.
Hold the center! We can't lose it!
We are losing too many transports! Do something!
You failed at protecting the convoy, you will be held accountable!
We are still losing trucks! Do something!
They destroyed our trucks! Take back the road!
We must warn the remaining convoy so they can take another route.
Excellent! Retreat to the prepared line of defense.
We have lost the anti-aircraft gun, we can't shoot down any aircraft!
We have lost a few trucks, but you completed the task!
To retreat, move your soldiers onto the road and you will leave this sector. Any soldier that remains fighting in the open will sacrifice himself here, covering your retreat.
We have almost reached our position.
What the hell?! The Fascists have already reached the first line of defense. Stand your ground! Move into position and hold the line!
The Germans are moving from the west towards the trucks! Protect the vehicles to the last man!
We regained control of the defense line!
The truck driver is down! Now the truck is a sitting duck!
They destroyed the truck, damn it! Do something about it!
We've managed to do our best holding this defensive perimeter, but we must now pull back to the second line of defense!
Hold the line at all costs!
We're losing ground too fast, damn it! We're pulling back to the second line of defense!
The Germans are coming from the northwest!
The Fascists are coming from the beach!
The enemy is advancing along the center, aim your guns towards the road!
The enemy has captured our first line!
I will grant you reinforcements. Don't waste them, and don't allow the enemy to destroy any of our convoys.
I will go to HQ with Belousov to report German movements. Belousov, get into the second truck!
I will go to HQ to report on the situation.
HQ allocated reinforcements to cover the column! Use the anti-aircraft gun to destroy the enemy fighter aircraft.
We are preparing the main defensive position. As soon as the column is safe, pull back!

It is nice to see you alive and well, comrade. We have a critical situation. The Germans broke through the defenses in the nearby sector and are dashing towards our position. Our right flank was completely obliterated.
Take command of several of my soldiers. I also transfer my medics to your command. Try to treat the wounded and stabilize the frontline!

On the south, German planes bombed the last convoy. Two cars loaded with wounded soldiers were left stranded. You must protect the vehicles from enemy attacks at any rate! Use the landscape as cover, and don't let the enemy kill our wounded!
They destroyed our line of defense! You were unable to cope with the task at hand. Traitor!

Great job, you regained control of the defense line. There is no time to waste. The main German forces can be here at any moment. Distribute the troops along the defense line. Try to make the surviving guns and tanks operational, the Germans will press us without mercy.

HQ reports it will take a considerable amount of time to evacuate. We need to delay the enemy for as long as possible and then retreat away from the sector. You will be informed of the progress of the evacuation.
They're hitting us hard! Take some of the reserve troops and plug in the gaps along the defensive line!
They're heading to the evacuation point across the beach! Don't let them get through!
You lost the second line of defense, now the Germans have nothing stopping them from reaching our ships!

The Black Sea fleet light cruiser 'Voroshilov' is nearby, they are ready to provide us fire support. Try to fire on large enemy troop concentrations, at this range the accuracy of the barrage will be low.
Our aircraft have reported enemy artillery movement into our sector. They will likely deploy them in the whereabouts to shoot at our naval vessels. I'll report the situation to headquarters!
Enemy artillery has begun to fire at our ships! We must stop them! Our comrades' blood is in your hands!
The Germans have broken through! You have failed to protect the evacuation point.
HQ is now granting you our last reserves to break through the Germans and destroy the enemy artillery!
The enemy plane has been hit! We're putting our air force to shame with our endless retreat!
Tank moving to the right flank!
Tank moving to the left flank!
German squad on the right flank!
We're fighting out in the open. Enemy aircraft will shred us to pieces.
Comrade commander, we have lost Voloshin's squad!
The convoy is on its way!
Another convoy is on its way!
We are under attack from that Messerschmitt! Shoot it down!
Enemy airplane incoming from the west!
Enemy fighter coming from the east!
Out of range... I hope he will not strafe our convoys...
The Fascists are coming at us once more!
We haven't lost any trucks! Great!
We fixed the first truck. It's heading out.
The second truck is also leaving!
The truck has left this area!
The trucks have left this area!
Artillery shelling, take cover! Lie down in your trenches!
The enemy is coming in from the coastline!
The last ship sailed away from the coast. A job well done, comrade!
Enemy artillery took up positions on the shore! It will take time to adjust their guns to fire. Something needs to be done immediately, commander.
Their artillery missed by a hundred meters! They are zeroing in fast!
The enemy has missed our ship by a mere couple of meters!
We destroyed the enemy battery! Our ships are safe!
Mine the approaches to the road
Dig trenches and foxholes to defend the road

Eventually, the Red Army evacuated what was left of the 44th Army by sea. A rearguard was left behind to cover the evacuation, which took place on the east beaches. Some 116,000 soldiers escaped. Later that summer, Sevastopol fell; but the Red Army would return in 1944 to take it all back.

Because you did not do enough to delay the Germans, they are now driving toward the east beaches! The evacuation will turn into a bloodbath. After that, the Germans will be able to cross into the Taman Peninsula almost unopposed. Their attack plan for next year can now be altered to include an army group marching on Maikop from just 300 km to the west.
Order soldiers to retreat to allied positions
Not a single truck should be destroyed
What the Germans call Operation Bustard Hunt is now underway. The Red Army tries to stop them, having built defensive lines stretching from coast to coast across the peninsula.
Destroy the enemy tank and infantry
Dig in and prepare the defensive line
Protect the retreating convoy from the enemy
Send a soldier to warn the convoy
Go to the frontline and take command
Get to the positions and find out about the situation
Take back control of the position and protect the trucks with the wounded
Hold the first line of defense
Hold the second line of defense
Defend the Soviet Evacuation from the Peninsula
Attack and destroy the enemy artillery battery
What has become of our beloved Stalingrad? The streets of the city are ruined… almost everything has been demolished.
Comrades, I've taken command of the 62nd Army. I tell you this - Stalingrad will decide our fate! I’ll either keep the fascists out of Stalingrad or die trying. There is no land beyond the Volga!
I do realise your men have been called forward without resupply. You need weapons and ammo. We are going to deal with this situation first. We know for a fact a German depot is nearby.
Your next objective is to take the strategic apartment building overlooking this entire area.

Due to our grueling losses, I have put into action Order 166: Offensives are to be organized into small groups with sub-machine guns, hand grenades, and anti-tank rifles. Taking this building is your assignment, Comrades. I will try to get reinforcements for you after the building is in your hands.
Good work Comrades. Take positions around this building. The Germans will surely want to take back such a strategic spot.
I am dispatching Lieutenant Afanasyev from the 3rd Machine Gun Company to reinforce your position. Sergeant Pavlov, you remain in command of this group. Keep your building safe!
I am sending a notorious sniper to reinforce your men, Comrade Pavlov. He is young, but has a reputation among the fascist hordes. Keep him alive and safe.
Comrades, engineering supplies have been found left behind by the Germans. I am ordering you to reinforce the approaches of the building to improve its defensive capabilities.
Make our defense unbreakable! All the furious attacks of the Fascist troops will shatter upon these obstacles just like sea waves are broken by granite rock!
That's it, Comrades. We are winning. Every German soldier must be made to feel that he is living under the muzzle of a Russian gun.
German artillery has been deployed very close to your position and they are threatening our landings on the Volga. I need you to take them out, Comrades!
Good work, Soldiers. I would not have believed such an inferno could open up on earth. Your men died but they did not retreat. Remarkable.
Enemies are within Pavlov's House and you've left it unprotected! I'll give you a minute to turn this situation over, or you're done! And don't let this happen again!

Excellent work! This was a remarkable display of leadership and tenacity. You have defied the odds and successfully prevented the fascists from taking the main prize of their campaign: Stalingrad. You are a true hero of the Soviet Union. Better get your uniform washed and pressed for a ceremony!

That is a dramatic end to a dramatic battle. What now? Do we let the fascists take control of Stalingrad? General Chuikov will not like this news. You will have to go in again and this time, hold on to the house. Don’t give up, there is no land beyond the Volga!

German army group B has reached Stalingrad, despite Stalin’s order 227 saying “not a step back”. Already in September, street fighting is a grim everyday reality.  The Soviet 62nd army, commanded by general Chuikov, is hanging on to a few small bridgeheads on the west bank of the Volga river.  If the Germans want to get to the Volga, they will need to get past Pavlov’s house first!  In this mission, General Chuikov will brief you on taking the house with your men. As soon as you have full control of the house, prepare every floor and every position for the inevitable next fascist attack. Hold the house long enough for the next wave of supplies to arrive. Show no mercy.  Za Rodinu!
Hold the building at all costs!
Take out the enemy artillery threatening the Volga landings
Treat Sergeant Yakov Pavlov before he bleeds to death!
Upon arrival to the village, I want the prisoners dealt with and the men gathered for a sweep of the marshes. The Command wants us to rat out a problematic partisan group.
Scheisse! I lost control of the steering... the brakes are also down god damn it!!
Go comrades, take cover and grab any weapon you find! Death to the fascist invaders!
Onward comrades! The supply truck is ours! Scavenge everything you can from it!
Germans! The Germans are leaving the village! They're coming this way!!
Comrade Commander, I don't think they have given our position away! It's not just the Germans. Some of our villagers have joined them too! The Fascists are forcing our own people against us!
Welcome to Obsich, comrades. I am in charge here. The Fascists are sending a lot of their convoys through these roads nowadays, we try to target the easy ones with supplies.
We could use your help! The Germans are doing something to our village. It has become a fortified supply nexus, they've reinforced the sector and we know nothing of our people. We fear the worst...
Agreed. Follow us! We'll take you to our hideout.

The German activity in the village is alarmingly high. There is a reckless German officer stationed there and the Soviet high command has requested we terminate him. All entrances are guarded. This Fascist swine is important!

With your men, we will attempt to infiltrate the village, take out the armor, and most importantly, do not let that Fascist officer escape alive! If we can strike a hard blow against the Hitlerite hordes, hopefully, they will leave our village alone.
What!? Impossible! Somebody has given away our hideout!
I should have never trusted you, traitors!
Shit! Hanomag! Flank that vehicle and get them from behind before that MG-42 kills us all!
There's ammo, weapons and equipment in the crates! Take what you need!
Great work comrades. Now our position is compromised. We must proceed with our plans of liberating Obsich and terminating the Fascist commanding officer!
Go! For the Motherland! Death to the fascist beast!
A drink, comrades! Henceforth, our village may remain free from the yoke of fascism!
The Fascists are missing the schedule, they are in haste. Ambush the supply vehicles and let the others go, I don't think they'll be after you.
Comrade, focus your attention only on the trucks!
Ignore the armor! We're only interested in the supply vehicles!
The enemy has brought mortars! You must eliminate them quickly!
The officer is trying to get away! You cannot let this happen at any rate!
I need your squad to move swiftly. Some of my men are acting as spotters in the village. Cut off any escape routes the officer may want to use. We will attack when you give us the signal.

If the officer is compromised, he will try to escape!! You must have all exits covered by the time you give us the attack signal. I will give you three of my best men to help you in this dangerous task.
Home sweet home! ...They left behind all the documents... How very interesting...
Convoys. Lots of them. It seems we're in one of the few available crossroads where they don't get completely stuck in the mud.
Every truck we stop... Every minute we delay them... It buys precious time for our comrades in the front line to stop the fascist advance!
Another column is coming soon! I'll keep you posted! I reckon you have a couple of minutes until its arrival! Find some mines or explosives around the village and prepare for them!
The enemy convoy is approaching from the northwest!
The Fascist column is approaching from the southwest!
Attention! The enemy convoy is arriving from the south!
My scouts can see the next German convoy has almost arrived on our doorstep! I will keep you posted.
Take down the trucks! They are our target! Let the armored vehicles through! We are no match for the fascist armor.
We'll join you, comrade. First, we need to get the hell out of here before the Germans know what hit them.
Stop this nonsense comrade! We've not betrayed you!
Take defensive positions! We will defend this place to the last man!
Our squad will ambush as many as we can! Keep us updated on the German’s movements!
Aha, what's this? We could work something out...

The Vitebsk gate would play an important part in the war. It enabled the partisans to disrupt supply lines more easily. Big battles were influenced by the partisans, such as the battle of Kursk. German supplies would never be safe again. Many partisans re-enlisted in the Red Army once their territory had been liberated, a feat to which they themselves had been instrumental.

Now that the German attack has succeeded, we can no longer use our exposed base. All equipment and supplies will have to be hauled through the marshes for dozens of kilometres. Losing this battle also means we will have to share our supplies with the villagers, who are now forced to leave their homes. We will not be able to block German reinforcements for a while. We can only hope this battle didn’t make us lose another one at the front.
Convoys of valuable Soviet POWs are brought back and forth for questioning and interning in camps. With the wet autumn underway, only a few roads remain serviceable.
Assist the partisans in eliminating the German convoy.
Follow the partisans to their dugout.
Drive the Germans out of Obsich.
Eliminate the enemy convoys, don't let any supply vehicle get through!
All defensive positions were lost to the enemy

Angled armor is extremely effective against lower caliber shells. While large calibers have better overmatching, the Panzer III's 50mm shells will have a very hard time penetrating your T-34's armor if you angle it correctly.
Your gun now has APCR rounds. They penetrate much further than regular rounds, but their smaller core deals less damage, they are uncommon, and the accuracy/penetration drop is stronger.

The enemy frontal armor is tough, and the APCR shells do not have as much normalization (they struggle against angled armor). This means you should immobilize the target and then reposition for a side shot with APCR.

Amongst the wealth of weaponry, it is easy to detect anti-tank troops, since their weapons appear with a red highlight on the 'Unit state icon'. There is a variety of AT weapons, some of which are also useful for anti-personnel.
Boxes scattered along the allied territory may contain ammunition and useful resources. You must use these calm moments before the storm to re-fit your soldiers for combat.

Vehicles and boxes may contain mines or other defensive equipment. You may drive these vehicles up to the front line to carry all the equipment - but remember to manually switch off the engine, so you will not arouse any suspicion.
Secret objectives unlock mission segments or open hidden features in every battle. In order to complete them, you must scan the map for unusual locations and spend time exploring.

Every scenario offers unique units. During the hardships of winter battles, it was usual to see skis being used as a platform for a variety of military equipment. You may switch weapons mounted on the shields through their inventory.
If you are ready, you can skip the defensive preparations by clicking on the right button.
Coming up right now comrade commissar!
Snow drifting on the horizon! The breeze also brings a distant rumble!

No! Don't be foolish comrade - mine the approaches to our anti-aircraft batteries. That is what they're after. If nothing stands between the Luftwaffe and us, Von Manstein will have their troops spectate an aerial massacre!
They're coming! Dig trenches! Prepare to defend!

The Germans will not risk losing too many tanks - they will advance through the river over tracks of previous vehicles that got across. They will also prioritize any AT equipment! Try to lure them into a trap!
Damn! That means they plan to use it to good effect. Comrades, place dynamite on the airstrip! Something tells me we'd better deny the Germans use of the airfield.
The artillery is much more accurate than before! This cannot be sustained! Someone must be directing their fire!
Sir, the defenses further back are not yet ready!
Welcome to our Motherland, fascist scum!
Comrade Commissar, the northern flank has been breached. They blew up the communication lines, sorry if the bad news could not be delivered earlier...
My soldiers will work on the barbed wire and inspect the trenches. You take care of the rest comrade!
Hell! All village perimeters have been lost!!!
I've had enough! The Germans already know we're here - I'm going to blow that detonator.
We do not have enough men to cover all the approaches to the village - we will need to reposition with each subsequent wave! The Germans will test all our positions!

We've retreated by 10 kilometers already and regrouped near this village - We have had a taste of them already. They know they don't have men to spare, so they advance cautiously with terrible effectiveness.
Hmm. Maybe they were the ones directing the fire.
Damn it! Like I thought... they're coming this way!
Grishenko, where is the bloody mining truck? Are we going to stop a panzer regiment scratching our asses out here?
Comrades! Listen carefully, we do not have much time.......
Very well. Let's go over it again. Surely the Germans will try ALL the approaches until they find a weak spot. I think it's our turn next...
Comrade, take command of the small outpost squad and do your best to withstand the Germans. Follow my instructions carefully.
They are scouting... Move in for a swift ambush. It would be unwise to reveal all our firepower on such a small group.
Let's see how those swine like our mines.
This is no time for complacency comrades. The Germans will not be gone for long. We must rearm and dig deeper...
We put this damaged tank back in action yesterday. Let's see if we can give those bastards a good impression!
Let some of them go! It may take them more time to come back if they really think we have an armored column with us!
I want all the reserves to gather around the village. Nightfall is approaching and we have the longest night of our lives ahead!
Comrades, time is of the essence.
The 2nd Guards Army is coming as we speak, we stand here alone until their arrival.
However, the Germans may be thinking the village is occupied by an entire army. The thick weather has not allowed for aerial reconnaissance from either side. We too do not know what awaits us.
I expect the enemy to attack in full force at dusk. We must do the impossible during the night. Prepare to defend against the fascist scum.
I want this village to be the last piece of the Motherland they see before we hammer the last nail in their coffins. Is that clear?
See if you can make some of our damaged units fit for action again. We have several abandoned vehicles around here.
I want ammunitions distributed and all supply reserves thrown into our front line! You will find them in the awnings.
We won't take a step back! We won't be leaving Gromoslavka - the fuel that is left can be used to create boobytraps. Blow the barrels when the Germans are close!
There are mines and other tools around the village! Find every piece of useful equipment!
It seems they will attack from the west first. Apparently, they want to take the airfield!
The enemy took the hill by the airfield!
The Fascists are advancing into the village! Hold the line!
Those pigs are securing positions on the south flank! Don't let them push you out!
Their main attack comes from the southwest - Hold on!
Enemy coming from the south! Hold the position!
We have lost the airfield perimeter to the enemy!
The high ground is ours again!
They have overrun our position at the village entrance! We have to push them out to the other side of the river!
Yes! The central perimeter is ours again! Make sure it stays that way!
Damn it! The enemy has driven us out of the southern sector! Counterattack!
The southern flank is ours again! Hold on to it!
Shoot the tracks off! Hit the flat surfaces, don't let them come close!!
Bloody hell! What on earth are those things?
What are they up to now??
It's pointless to stay here! We have to fall back!
The Germans advance cautiously. While they move up their forces we will help the regiment finish the village defenses.
Comrade, you might want to reposition that AT-gun. The Germans will take according measures! I remind you these are not recruits we're dealing with.
Comrades, gather around, we have one more surprise planned for the Germans.
I trust you with the command of our only AT-gun in the sector.
We have found a great position for it, comrade, it is on higher ground and out of sight from the road.

It is intentionally concealed behind the trees. This is why we have placed land mines amongst the shrubberies. The detonator is ready by the mortar position. Wait until the fascists bring armored vehicles, and then, press the detonator!
What was that? You just completely wasted the element of surprise!
Gun's ready! Now let's shred those swine to bits!

Damn it! We were supposed to keep the fuel from falling into enemy hands. In fact, we should not let them use this airfield at all!! They would be close enough to Stalingrad to overcome our blockade and supply their troops!
Comrade Commissar! What makes you think the Germans won't attack in full force!?
Comrade Commissar, we brought mines with us! Should we mine the roads to the village?
Comrade Commissar - snow dust is visible on the horizon!
They... look like tough guys, comrade Commissar!
What the hell? Did this truck slide on the ice while evacuating fuel?

Helped by appalling weather and their growing battle experience, the Red Army held the line at Gromoslavka. The 6th Army would have to soldier on without help, short of ammunition and food - despite an attempt to supply the pocket from the air. The only relief operation came to a standstill  at the hands of the 51st Army, shattering the false hopes of the Germans inside the Stalingrad pocket. In early February 1943, they surrendered.

The Germans break through to the north as a result of this battle. You should have held the village! Now the Germans can  break out and save hundreds of thousands of their comrades. The next spring they will be back at the front and all hope of a counteroffensive is now lost!

The situation at Stalingrad is hopeless for the encircled Germans. They start an offensive from the south to relieve their trapped army. All eyes are now on the 51st Army, which stands between them and Stalingrad.
Drive the Germans out of the village
Demolish the foliage when heavy armored vehicles arrive and take control of the gun.
Fortify the positions in the village and prepare for the enemy attack!
Blow up the airstrip to prevent German reinforcements from landing.
Comrades, we have received intelligence that confirms the fascist summer offensive will start today!
We have dug the most comprehensive fortification lines ever seen in the history of warfare. We are ready to stop the hitlerite hordes and drive them back to Berlin!
We've been ordered to lay as many mines as possible in preparation for the fascist attack. Get to work, soldiers!
