Daybreak on D-Day. The 82nd Airborne is on the ground in Normandy. Not everything went right; the cloud base over the drop zone and the German Flak was dense. You have spent hours of darkness trying to find your comrades, and after a short headcount, it’s clear that this will be one hell of a day.    Your group is tasked to take the bridge at La Fière and hold it until the US Army arrives from Utah Beach.     Your task is vital; once you take the bridge, the enemy can no longer approach St. Mère-Église from the west, or reach the roads to the invasion beaches.   Good luck!
Capture the manor and secure the bridge!
Defend the bridge and the manor!
Place at least four anti-tank mines on the road.
(Secret objective) Stop the enemy soldier on a bike before he alarms a nearby garrison.
(Secret objective) Use the radio to call in reinforcements.
Move men! Get out of the ditch! Go!
The crossroads are secure! Move north along the road to the center of town. Let's move out!
We've got no cover here! Move! Move!
We need to hit those mortars fast, or they'll rip us apart!
Look alive! A fresh squad here to join the fight.
Gardens on the right are secure!
We have managed to clear everything south of this railway! We've observed enemy movement in the town, they appear to be preparing to counterattack.
Our Weapons Platoon has caught up to us. Get them set in and prepare to defend our position.
Friendly glider troops coming from the North-West!
We've got orders to set up defenses on the high ground to the west of town. We're not going to wait around here for another counterattack.
Well you just take it easy, Lip. We'll get you out of here and back to England.
Don't worry about me, Sir. I'll be back before long.
Hey, check this out! Jerry was too busy runnin’ to take this with ‘em!
This area of town is secure! What do we have planned next, Sir?
Well done! With Carentan secured, our forces at Omaha and Utah are now linked. With this continuous beachhead, our forces can break out and take control of the Cotentin peninsula.
We failed! Carentan remains in German hands, preventing our forces on Utah and Omaha beaches from linking up. You must try again!

It's been almost a week since you parachuted into France, and it’s been one hell of a week. The Germans are not ready to give up Normandy, and several fierce counterattacks have proven that this battle is far from over.    It’s clear that whoever holds Carentan, holds the key to the Cotentin peninsula. If the 101st takes Carentan, our Utah and Omaha Beach forces can unite to form a continuous front.    Your regiment, the 506th PIR, will approach Carentan from the south. Your orders are to take the Carentan railway station. In support of your push, the 401st Glider Infantry Regiment will attack from the opposite side of town.   Good luck!
Neutralize the enemy MG42 and clear the crossroads!
Clear the road heading to the center of Carentan!
Neutralize enemy mortars in the gardens!
Defend your position until reinforcements arrive!
Neutralize enemy mortars in the town!
Link up with allied Glider troops and capture enemy HQ!
(Secret Objective #1) Find the German rocket artillery.
Treat Lt. Winters before he bleeds to death!
Easy Company! Our scouts reported that an enemy formation is coming our way and will be here soon!
Take up defensive positions along these hedgerows. Reinforce them if you need to. Use the mines to cover possible enemy approaches.
Hold your ground and let them come to us. Hang tough, men!
The enemy has trapped our scout team behind their lines. They’ve held up in this compound!
Third squad! Break through the German line, link up with the scout team, and fall back before the enemy attack arrives.
Come on, Blithe! Stand up! Get on your feet, soldier! Fire your weapon, Blithe!
Here they come! Get ready, soldiers!
I hear tank tracks in the distance! Enemy armor inbound!
We need to neutralize the German armor. Bazooka teams, flank and destroy them!
We've repelled the enemy assault! Now that we have armor, it's time to go on the offensive.
No time to rest, let's push 'em back!
Well done! Those German mortars are done for!
You guys made it just in time. I thought we were goners for sure! If you help me get back to HQ, I can call for additional support with my radio.

Easy Company successfully repelled the German attack with support from the 2nd Armored Division. With the German attackers routed, the Allies were able to push west and cut off the German forces in the Cotentin Peninsula from German-occupied France.
Easy Company was destroyed by the Germans while defending its position west of Carentan. Now, nothing stands in the way of the German advance towards Carentan. You must try again!
Press on this button to skip the preparation countdown and move on to the next part of the mission.

The 101st has been in action constantly since the jump into Normandy over a week ago. After clearing Carentan yesterday, it’s time to push forward and capitalize on this victory.    Easy company will be covering the extreme right flank. Headquarters has sent scouts forward along the axis of advance. Depending on what they report, we will proceed accordingly. Report to the 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment for further orders and prepare for what could be a bloody battle.   Good luck!
Prepare a defense line along the hedgerow!
Save the radio operator from the scout team.
Escort the radio operator to your HQ for additional support.
Hold your position and defend the HQ!
Clear the remaining enemy troops from the battlefield!
Treat Lt. Winters before he bleeds to death!

Operation Market Garden, a daring combined attack by the 1st Allied Airborne Army and 30 Corps, starts today. Allied Airborne troops are to be dropped at the main objectives; they must secure multiple bridges and hold them until the ground forces arrive.    To achieve this goal, nine road bridges must be secured to allow 30 Corps to drive all the way to Arnhem. You have been dropped near Nijmegen with the 82nd “All American” Airborne Division. After the drop, your objective is to secure the road bridge.    Moving north, you need to advance through the city. The Germans are still in positions between you and the road bridge. You’ll have to clear them out before making your next move.   Good luck!
Great job! This mission was difficult, but you have overcome incredible odds. The crossing was murderous, but the Nijmegen Bridge is secure, and it’s the 82nd that did it!

We can’t afford failure here! That bridge is the one thing we need to secure - there is no way around it. We must go in again; this time, we must take it at any cost or risk the whole operation failing.
Alright, soldiers! Our objective is ahead of us, the Waal bridge!
We need to eliminate German strong points in the area. Secure St. Steven's church, the main intersection, and the docks.
Even after the bombardment, German resistance is stronger than expected. We need to find another direction to approach the bridge.
Half of our force will cross the river in an attempt to secure the bridge from the other side. The remaining half will stay here and defend our foothold in the church!
We've made it across! Let's clear the area and secure the river bank!
Good work! Now we can cut the Germans off by capturing the northern side of the bridge!
Those 88s are between us and the bridge! Let's knock 'em out!
The northern end of the bridge is secured!
The British tanks are here! We can use their help to push through the city!
We must secure Valkhof Park before we can take control of the bridge. Push forward, men!
Radio Op here, Sir! What do you need me to do?
We could use an airstrike on the German stronghold in the park. Move up close to where you can observe the park and radio it in.
They've got their heading. Airstrike is on its way!
Cross the river using the boats!
Secure the northern end of the bridge!
Move the radio operator to one of the designated places to call in an airstrike.
Panzers! I see German armor coming from the north!
Get to defensive positions! We have to protect our supply trucks!
Look alive! More Krauts are coming from along the highway!
A Panther! Gun crew, aim for a weak spot, or it will kill us!
Our 57 mil is down! Someone deal with that Panther!
Looks like they've had enough! We need to ensure the highway ahead is clear of any Germans.
Continue to protect our trucks. They must deliver supplies to our troops!
German tank destroyers are operating nearby. Locate and destroy them.
We have been granted limited artillery support from a nearby battery. One high-explosive and two smoke barrages are available.
We need to clear any remaining enemies from the village and nearby woods.
Good job! The enemy tank destroyers won't threaten our convoys anymore!
The highway is clear of enemy troops! Let's get those trucks moving!
Excellent work! You have thwarted the enemy’s attempts to take Highway 69. The road to Arnhem is still open to XXX Corps. Congratulations, soldier!
Losing this part of the highway to the Germans will delay the operation. It’s absolutely necessary to take back the road. You must try again!

Having secured Veghel five days ago, the 101st is thrown into battle once more. The allied ground forces approach from the south along Highway 69, which is the only road available for their advance.    If the British XXX Corps is to succeed, you need to fend off any enemy attacks and prevent the narrow stretch of highway from falling into German hands.    With the success of Operation Market Garden hanging in the balance, the importance of your task cannot be overstated.   Good luck!
Protect the supply trucks (at least 3 must survive)
Clear the enemies from the highway!
Find and neutralize German tank destroyers!
Escort the supply trucks safely to the end of the highway (at least 3 trucks must get there).
Alright troopers! It sounds like 10th Armored is still fighting for the village! We need to get in there!
We need to help Major Desobry clear the Germans out of Noville!
You arrived just in time! The Germans broke our line and threatened our HQ.
Now that we've pushed them back, we can rebuild our defenses.
The attack damaged much of our equipment. We need to repair everything we can. We are also low on ammo. Scrounge up any supplies you can find.
You heard what the Major said. Let's get to work! We need to rebuild our defense line before Jerry attacks again!
We need to get these tanks and cannons operational quickly!
Take mines from the box and plant them out in front of our lines. It will be easier to take out enemy tanks when they are immobilized!
There are fuel and ammo trucks nearby. We should use them to resupply our equipment.
We need to take out those Kraut rocket launchers before they blast us to bits!
Friendly tank destroyers approaching, just in time!
They've flanked us! The Germans are attacking from the southeast!
They are running away! Well done!
The minefields will help slow any incoming German armor!
Well done! You have bought enough time for the rest of the 101st to set up defenses and prepare for a German attack. You may have made the difference between keeping or losing Bastogne.

Our comrades in Bastogne will now face the entire German force unprepared. If only you could have bought them some more time! Bastogne will fall, and the Germans will have an open road to the Meuse River. You must try again!

Just three days ago, a German surprise offensive smashed through the allied lines in the Ardennes. Initially, they advance rapidly. They aim to take Antwerp. The German 5th army has orders to cross the Meuse River at Dinant and Namur, without which a push to Antwerp is simply out of the question.    To get to those bridges, they will need to take Bastogne. The 2nd Panzer Division intends to pass through Noville to outflank the Bastogne defenders from the north.   However, in Noville, a small force from the 10th armored division blocks their way. The first battalion of the 506th PIR moves forward to reinforce them.   Good luck!
Lay mines in front of the defense line before the attack starts (at least 50 mines).
Time left before another enemy attack:
The bridge shouldn't be much farther... In fact, I can see it now.
Wait, I see movement by the bridge!
Hold your fire until they right on us!
Well, they didn't put up much of a fight, but now they know we're here...
Let's move out and take back our fuel depot!
Look! They are keeping prisoners in that barn! We need to free our boys!
We've secured the fuel depot! Check the area for any heavy weapons or equipment we can use.
Thanks for rescuing us! Those Krauts came out of nowhere!
Don’t mention it. Just grab a weapon and fall in.
See that radio tower by the buildings to the north? That’s not supposed to be there. Let’s go have a look.
The tower is ours!... I hear Kraut chatter coming from the radio. Does anyone speak German?
I speak some German, Sir! I’ll see if I can catch what they’re saying.
Well, Sir, if I understand them correctly, a German armored column is almost here, at the river crossing!
Men! There is no time to waste! We need to set up a defense at the bridge immediately.
Place explosives under the bridge in case we cannot hold our position. We'll need to destroy the bridge as a last resort.
I'll take care of the explosives, Sir! Just give me some time!
Explosive planted! One more to go!
Shit! They killed him! Now, we cannot destroy the bridge as a last resort!
Excellent! Destroying the bridge is our last resort. If at all possible, we need to keep the crossing open.
Hold the bridge at all costs, men! We cannot let any German armor cross!
A few tank destroyers have come to help us hold the crossing!
More German armor approaching! If we cannot stop them, now's a good time to blow the bridge!
Congratulations! The Germans did not get through! They’ve been denied the precious fuel they needed, and now all they can do is look for another bridge to go west.
Kampfgruppe Peiper now has open roads up to the Meuse River. With all of the fuel they’ve captured, they just might get all the way to Antwerp. You must try again!

The Germans have launched a massive surprise attack in the Ardennes. On their right flank, the route to Brussels leads past Elsenborn Ridge, which dominates the area. The 277th Volksgrenadier Division is sent to take the ridge and the villages around it. Meanwhile, Kampfgruppe Peiper continues west in the Amblève valley.    The 82nd Airborne Division is one of a few US units available to block the German advance. The situation is desperate. If the Germans cross here, they will acquire all the fuel they need from the local fuel depot.    That’s why you have been brought here. Secure the bridge and ensure that the Germans cannot use it.   Good luck!
Protect the soldier planting explosives under the bridge!
(Secret objective) Secure all the fuel trucks intact!
(Secret objective) Repel the enemy attack without blowing up the bridge!
Protect the soldier planting the explosives under the bridge:
The situation in Bastogne is desperate...
We've been holding out for days, surrounded by the enemy with no supplies coming through.
The men are worn down to the bone; tired, hungry, and cold. Ammunition is running low, and our medics can barely keep up with the wounded.
There's no way to fall back, no room to maneuver. The noose tightens every day we stay here, but we won't give up Bastogne.
Our planes dropped supplies into no-man's land!
We could really use whatever is in those drops!
Soldier! Use the truck to recover everything you can from the supply drops before the Krauts do!
There they are! Christmas presents from Uncle Sam!
A box full of mines! Jerry won't know what hit 'em!
We got some .30cals and ammo here!
Looks like we got it all! Let's get back to our lines!
The Germans captured the air drops before we could!
Now let’s finish preparing those defenses. Every second counts. Take the explosives from this crate...
When the Krauts use the road, we'll detonate the explosive charges remotely.
Jerry's Christmas present is all wrapped up and ready to go!
Dawn’s almost here! Get those airdrop supplies handed out and prepare for the enemy assault.
The sun is rising. Get ready, men!
Enemy vehicles are coming down the main road! We should use the explosives to take them out! Get ready to trigger the charges!
General McAuliffe has granted us artillery support.
They are running away! Is that all they got?!
German armor broke through! They are behind us!
Shit! Turn around, men! We need to stop the Krauts from reaching the Command Post!
Soldiers! Shift positions and form a new defensive line around Headquarters. We must protect it!
Aw Nuts! The artillery battery is under attack. No more artillery support until we deal with this!
There are two armored units in your area. Choose one to reinforce you.
Well done. We've stopped their attack, and the HQ is still standing.
The remaining Germans have set up defensive positions in the village. We need to clear it!
Reinforcements have arrived! Let's take back the village!
Enemy attack dealt with. The artillery battery is operational!

Excellent work! The Germans failed to break through our lines and reach Bastogne. For now, the road to Antwerp remains outside the German's reach. This may prove to be a pivotal point in stopping the entire German offensive.
We failed to keep the Germans from capturing Bastogne. Now, they can waltz right through town and continue west. The road to Antwerp is open to them unless you try again!

The fierce struggle playing out in the Ardennes is reaching a critical phase. The Germans urgently need to take Bastogne. Right now, the town is completely surrounded by the German 5th army, led by von Manteuffel.    The German forces have offered terms of surrender, to which General McAuliffe has responded with a single word: NUTS! The screaming eagles will have to hold out. The Germans will probably start a massive attack at dawn; so there is some time to prepare for the onslaught, and you need to do everything within your power to get dug in and get organized. Your sector is just outside Bastogne, covering a road that leads into the town. Hold that road at any cost!   Good luck!
Secure the supplies before the enemy does!
Put the supplies into the truck and return to our lines.
Plant the explosives along the road, in the indicated area.
Hold your line in the forest!
Stop the German tanks and protect the HQ!
Clear the remaining enemies in the village!
(Secret Objective #1): Repair and crew the damaged howitzer!
Time before the Germans find the supply drops.
Bahrendorf is ours. Now, we must secure Drethem and the surrounding area before we can cross the river.
Let's send a patrol to Drethem to see if there are any enemy forces in the area.
We should take a look at that farmhouse as well.
*Shit*, the Americans are here. Please! You must leave this place!
Why do you say that? What's got you worried?
There are fanatical troops in the surrounding area. They are observing us. They are observing the whole area!
Junger Mann, we cannot be seen helping you, nor do we want to be caught in the middle of a fight. Not with them! Not here! *God Help Us!*
Listen up, men! Set up a defensive perimeter around the village and stay alert! There could be more stubborn Krauts nearby.
We need to get these civilians out of harm's way. Let's use one of these trucks to evacuate them back to Bahrendorf.
The civilians should be safe now!
Thank you for saving us! But please, just turn around! As long as you can and spare your men! And spare my village! This war - it is already over.
Move out! Secure the remaining areas on our side of the river!
Due to the poor weather conditions, we cannot use our aircraft, but we can use a nearby artillery battery to strike the enemy.

At last! You have reached the Elbe, and the war is as good as over. Those civilians will be very thankful, and you’ve done a great job to master a challenging situation. You have gloriously completed a campaign that was long and difficult. Maybe High Command will finally send you for some R & R, or maybe you can even go home? Time will tell. One thing is sure: you have earned a reputation of legendary proportions. Excellent work, soldier!

That’s very unfortunate. This kind of failure hasn’t happened in a long time. But maybe the circumstances were too unusual and too complicated this time. Maybe that’s what caused your mistakes. Your record shows you should be able to get this right. You should try again!

After the Battle of the Bulge, and after helping to secure the Ruhr, the 82nd Airborne Division is driving into Germany. Anyone in their right mind can see that the war is ending. Yet, any Germans caught waving a white flag still run the risk of being executed on the spot.    The 82nd knows full well what might still happen as it enters the hamlet of Bahrendorf. Your unit advances to Drethem, which is on the Elbe River. After taking Drethem, crossing the river can be considered only if the area is secure.   Good luck!
Evacuate the civilians to safety. (All 10 must survive)
Clear all the enemy resistance on this side of the Elbe River.
Strategic location was retaken by enemy soldiers!
Enemy artillery incoming! On the ground!
Repair and recover this abandoned enemy tank!
Air bombing of the selected area
Deploy your reinforcements on the battlefield

The phony war has erupted into Blitzkrieg! The Germans invade the Netherlands and Belgium on May 10th. What the Germans call “Fall Gelb” is underway.  You have been ordered north with your unit to reinforce the Dyle line.  Your part of the line is at a bridge, not far from Louvain. The Germans will definitely want to use this bridge to get to Brussels, so this is a key position in the Dyle line.
We have shown them what to expect from the British Expeditionary force. We might be retreating from the battle today, but we bought ourselves and our allies some more time.
That is rather unfortunate, we should have held the line here. Because we haven’t stopped this brutal attack, Jerry can now continue his drive into Belgium and toward France, unfortunately.
The 6-inch howitzer has arrived. We got only one chance, don’t screw this up!
Jerry has spotted our gun! They will open fire in no time, change the position of the bloody howitzer, quickly!
Nice shot, one gun down. Two left!
Brillant, two guns down. One left!
The enemy artillery is now silent, great job!
Bloody hell, we just lost our howitzer! I don’t know how but you have to find an alternative way to deal with the German artillery.
The anti-air Vickers has arrived. We got only one chance, don’t screw this up!
The pilot has spotted our anti-air vehicle! Change its position, quickly!
Nice shot, this plane is down.
Watch out, there comes another one! It’s engaging your anti-air vehicle!
Brilliant shot but there is a third plane approaching your location, deal with it!
I think it was the last of ‘em. Good job.
Blimey, we just lost our anti-air vehicle! I don’t know how but you have to find an alternative way to deal with the Luftwaffe.
The artillery observer has arrived. Don’t let Jerry spot him. We got only one chance, make this a good one!
Watch out, the observer has been spotted!
Great, this anti-air gun will not bother us anymore!
Brilliant, the AT gun is destroyed.
Excellent, the guns have been destroyed.
Dammit, the observer has been killed! Find another way to destroy the emplacements!
Matilda has arrived. We got only one chance, don’t screw this up!
The Panzers have spotted our tank, you have to deal with ‘em, quickly!
Brilliant, one Panzer down, destroy the second one!
Great job, both tanks have been destroyed!
Blimey, we lost our tank! I hope you still have some 2-pounders at your disposal.
He’s gone. Could’ve saved him… That medic’s yours now. Do better next time.
Alright, he’ll make it. Bet this lad won’t forget your help for the rest of his life.
Williams, I need one more hand on this one, quick!
…Honestly, I’m sick of marching and digging trenches. And this heat… I swear, mate, it’s even worse than Kenya, back when I was on assignment. At least I had better company there. A lovely Mathilda…
Look at that, they even named that clanking monster in her honour. I’ve never told you about that trip, have I?
For Christ’s sake, Williams. Can you shut it for once? We’re all bloody sick of your stories.
Take it easy, Stu. I’m just trying to lift your spirits. You’re looking far too knackered for our little continental adventure. What’s wrong, ja? Scared of the Jerries?
Well spotted, genius. You are not even slightly bothered that the bloody Luftwaffe doesn’t let us sleep more than an hour a night? We’re all knackered, alright?
Shh, keep it down. The Captain seems really stressed today.

We’re alright for now. They’ve decided to send another company forward. We’re not going with this column. We need to double-check for potential gaps in our lines. Given the news, we might not be here much longer… But let’s prepare for the worst.
And for God’s sake, get that bloody 2-pounder out of the middle of the path already.
We’re not? I thought the frontline was going to stay static again. Just like last month. And the month before that. And half a bloody year ago... You know, Sir.
I reckon our luck has left us for now. It’s... it’s a bloody mess out there. But we’ll be fine. We will. Just… Just do your thing, gentlemen.
Hawkins! Christ, we lost one of our medics!
Williams! What the hell are you doing?! That medic is a goner!
Bloody hell, Crosby is down! We need to fall back, now!
Shit… They’re just gone… One strike and that’s it…
I need you to focus, men. There must be someone who has managed to find cover. I know that sending a small group like yours is risky but the Luftwaffe leaves me no choice.

Lieutenant Williams, your objective is to secure the area in case Jerry decides to scavenge the wrecks. No way those planes knew the convoy’s location without someone guiding ‘em from the ground. There should be some scout rats, for sure.

Corporal Crosby, you’re in charge of the medical team. Search for survivors and provide assistance. Williams, cover the medics at all costs. Report me when you’re ready for evacuation and I’ll send a lorry for the wounded. I can’t do it right now, the skies are too hot. Out.
Gosh… No one warned about the smell… Look at ‘em… They’re all… Burnt… I feel so sick.
It’ll be fine, alright? Pull yourself together. Keep an eye out for cover in case Jerry returns.
Fuck! I just… I just touched his fucking skin and…
Hey, take it easy mate. Think of something good. You'll be so bloody telling me about that Matilda girl of yours when we get out of here.
We’ve got company from the north!
Williams, we heard gunfire. What’s going on? Over.
Light German infantry approaching from multiple directions. We’ve found wounded, Crosby and his team are treating ‘em. Over.
Copy that, sending help to you. Out.
Enemy vehicle coming from the north, take it down!
Enemy aircraft! Everyone, get the hell down!
Man… That was a recon plane… Means the whole bloody German army knows we’re here. Crosby, get it done! Quickly!
We’re good to go. Williams, call it in!
Captain, this is Williams. We’re ready for an evacuation. The skies are clear at the moment, over.
Understood, Lieutenant. Lorry’s on the way, it’s three minutes away. Good work, lads. Out.
Lorry is ready! Crosby, get the wounded into it, now!
Everyone in, let’s get the hell out of here!
We’ll follow behind. Get ‘em to safety. See you on the other side.
Just need a bit more time. Keep us covered.
I’m out of ammo! Think I’ve seen an ammunition crate on the road, let’s have a peek.
Lads, listen up! The Huns are even closer to the Dyle River than we thought. We still have some time to prepare the defense. Use it to reinforce our positions.
Here they are, pushing our central positions! Hold your ground!
We weren’t trained for this kind of defence! Why are they hammering one spot instead of pushing along the whole frontline?
Probably their famous tactics they are using right now. One hard push in a vulnerable direction. Watch your less-protected areas!
I’ve managed to get through to HQ. They’re willing to send reinforcements, but only to cover our losses. Resources are very tight, so don’t expect anything extra.
Sir, did they tell you the latest information on the frontline? What’s happening?
From what I can tell… We’re exceeding the expectations so far. Keep it that way.
We slowed ‘em down, lads! Now destroy the remaining enemy vehicles!

Jerry has taken control of our northern flank! I am sending our last reserves to re-capture these positions before our whole entire defense falls. Lieutenant Williams, I need you to provide support for their counter-attack.
The enemy has brought in their heavy guns! My forces will not be able to counter attack while the howitzers are still operational. We have to deal with ‘em first.
There is a Jerry plane hanging about! It makes no sense to attack while Jerry has close air support. My forces have no anti-air equipment, so you guys have to deal with it on your own.

The enemy has brought in their emplacements! The AT and AA guns must be destroyed first. My forces will not be able to counter attack while the guns are still operational. We have to deal with those first.
The enemy has brought in their tanks! These tanks must be destroyed first. My forces have no anti-tank weapons, so you guys have to deal with ‘em on your own.
My lads are ready to advance to the German positions. Give me a signal once you’re ready.

We still have a royal ace up our sleeve, though. I am granting you access to a 6-inch howitzer for counter artillery combat. We only have one, so please be careful with this old lady. The Jerries will most likely open fire in response after a single shot, that’s why you have to put the Morris carrier to good use. Change your position after every shot.

We still have a royal ace up our sleeve, though. I am granting you access to an ack-ack tank to take this bloody plane down. We only have one, so please be careful with this lad. The pilot will most likely try to take this vehicle down once he spots it, so be careful and change your position as often as you can.

We still have a royal ace up our sleeve, though. I am granting you access to an artillery observer to provide exact coordinates to our artillery. Make the ground tremble under their feet. We only have one specialist, so make sure Jerry does not spot him.

We still have a royal ace up our sleeve, though. I am granting you access to a Matilda II tank which is capable of taking out both Panzers. We only have one, so please be careful with this young lady. However, keep your distance from the Jerries, we don’t know how they might respond.
The northern flank is under our control again. Brilliant job, everyone!
Seems like we stopped their advance…
I reckon we did… So, what’s the next step?
Blimey, the water’s lovely and warm today. Now if only we could get a couple of girls from the village to join us, that’d be just perfect.
I wasn’t much for saying thank you back then. Just thought none of us would make it out alive anyway.
Don’t mention. And sorry for being a pain in the ass with those stories I’ve told a hundred times. Just trying to keep your spirits up.
So… You mentioned Kenya, if I recall?
Oh yeah. You know what my uncle told me before I went? Said, “It’s like India, only with golf, lions, and less…” You know what they say about it… Bloody romantic, innit?
Oh, right… Here we go again…

He wasn’t joking. The whole family said the same thing: “Don’t come back without a lion’s head, or you’re just a tourist in uniform.” To them, no lion means no courage. And when you're the youngest son with no title and no estate… Well, there aren’t many ways to prove yourself.
So… did you actually get one?

Sort of. They assigned me a “gun bearer”. Local lad about my age. Poor bloke’s job was to carry my kit around. Felt bloody strange… Like some medieval knight with a squire behind me. Except he was doing it to feed three kids.
Didn’t know His Majesty Lord Williams felt so kindly toward us dirty peasants.

He barely did any “gun bearing”, to be fair. Carried my bags to the pub on day one, and that was about it. After that, he was more like a guide. We drank Pombe most of the time. That’s the local stuff. Made from sorghum and bananas. It was good after three pints, though.
Sounds like you really went native.

Too right. It’s much better than listening to my fellow Britons moaning all day “Locals lack discipline,” “I miss proper football,” “Where’s the bloody gin…” All that, while downing G&Ts like water. I was done with it. I just wanted some peace.
That sounds imperial enough. So… did you ever actually go after a lion?

Course I didn’t. I’m not daft enough to leave a good pub for the bloody savannah. Bought a lion’s head off some merchant before I sailed home. Gave the gun bearer a solid tip and called it a day. What’s the point, really? Chasing animals to prove something a bunch of dead men once wrote in a book?

So… Where was I? Ah, right. One night at that pub, me and my guide were watching the sunset, sipping Pombe… You should’ve seen those sunsets, Stuey. So bloody beautiful, I almost wrote a poem. For someone I’ll tell you about in a second…
So we’re downing, I don’t know, our fifth drink, and out of nowhere, this girl walks round the corner, right into the light of the sunset…
Lord Williams, sorry to interrupt your Shakespearean memoirs, but weren’t you due at the commanders’ briefing two minutes ago? Where, unless I’m mistaken, everyone’s already waiting?
Oh, bloody hell! Sorry, sir! I’ll tell you about Matilda later.
Christ… Didn’t expect Jerry to have that many tanks. No one told us about it. And even after this whole mess… We’re just leaving. I don’t know, it feels like it was for nothing.
But we stopped them, didn’t we? Maybe some lads from other battalions will be thankful for that.
We’ve been through bloody hell, mate. And that’s just today. Why the hell did Jerry even invade Belgium? They could’ve kept sitting on their asses and… not start this whole thing…
Well, I’ve heard the Russians are helping Jerry with fuel and industrial crap. Maybe that’ll push Winnie to strike a deal with Jerry and we’ll be home sooner than we think.
You heard where we’re heading next?
Some place in… Ehm, I don’t recall it, these French names are unpronounceable. Don’t think it even matters, let’s just make it ‘till the end.
You know… If Kenya taught me one thing, it’s how to enjoy the moment. Even if you’re stuck in a bloody, smelly, godforsaken quagmire. We’re fine for now. So shut up and enjoy the bloody view, Stuey.
Oi, what’s the deal with these ancient things?
These bunkers were built in the 30s. I don’t think they’re really useful. Maybe it's worth looking around to find some ancient stuff though.
You’re really one of a kind, huh? I’m not a doctor but throwing grenades when you’re in a bunker is not the smartest idea.

The Battle of France is reaching a critical stage. The German thrust through the Ardennes forest has been very successful, as their armored spearhead reaches the Channel coast near Abbeville on this day.   The Allies must counterattack to cut off the German breakthrough, or face certain defeat.   The British will counterattack from Arras today, with almost all of their remaining armor.   After a stop at Vimy you have now reached the starting line.   The fate of France - and that of the entire BEF - depends on this counterattack. You have to stop the Germans at all costs!

Well done, we have well and truly given the Germans something to think about! This will undoubtedly raise morale among the troops. Even if we didn’t stop the German advance, at least we slowed it down.
This counts as a costly failure; because we allowed our attack to be stopped, the Germans can now continue the encirclement of our main force. We must regroup and try again, after reporting to HQ.
Bloody hell… We failed to secure our field HQ! you need to go back and get another effort going!
You must hold your field HQ!
Punch a hole in the enemy position and drive north!
Welcome back to the front line, Lieutenant! This is our field HQ, it must remain in our control!
Counter-attack is in full swing, a swift assault is necessary to breach through the German lines.
Be quick, be decisive, and try not to lose too many men! Use the terrain to your advantage.
More reinforcements will become available as you progress with your assault!

Thanks for coming to our aid Lieutenant! We are under your command now.
We must hold our command post! There is no room for surrender!
Bloody hell! One of our tanks and trucks got lost and knocked out. We should try and recover this tank!
Major! Now you can request an airstrike.

Ever since the Germans broke through at Sedan three weeks ago, the Allies have been on the back foot.  Calais fell on the 27th, and Belgium capitulated on the 28th. The perimeter around Dunkirk is shrinking, and an attack on the remaining allied forces seems to be a matter of time only.  The Germans are pushing in on the shrinking perimeter from all sides, including from the air.  Today, it’s up to you and your comrades to buy the evacuation operation more time and to keep the Germans away from the beach as far as possible.
British Expeditionary Force, Armée de Terre
Your tenacity and courage have saved many lives today. The British empire will be able to continue the fight another day as the last country in Europe fighting against Germany.
Operation Dynamo has not been very successful, and it remains to be seen whether we will stay in the war - or surrender.
With all due respect, Sir, but you only won because Cliff Bastin was out half the season.
Keep telling yourself that. Everton didn’t need Bastin to lift the cup.
Lawton just had one flashy season. He’d never last against Arsenal’s back line in their prime!
We have more of these flyers than we do toilet paper… They really want us to wave the white flag.
God help us if Jerry gets his hands on us…
Let’s just… Let’s just keep moving…
Sir… Haven’t you heard what they do to prisoners?
I’ve only heard the rumors, same as you.
Is it true they use prisoners as bloody human shields?
Where did you hear that, Corporal? Same place you heard the Gunners were still the best in England?
The whole company is talking about this. And there's worse… Have you heard what the French are saying?
Alright, Corporal, let’s just hope we don’t find out.
They’ve sent civilian boats? Well, I reckon it’s better than nothing.
There you are, lieutenant! Over here, I’ve got a job for you.
Set up the first line of defense at the double. Our engineers are busy sabotaging the vehicles to prevent them from falling into enemy hands. We have to hold the Germans here until they are done.
Calling this situation critical is an understatement. The evacuation is far from complete and the enemy may strike any second.
During the retreat we left a lot of weapons and ammunition in these crates. Take a look inside them.
Sir, where are the rest of the gun crews?
We have a couple of AT guns but… Not enough trained personnel to operate them.
They’re most likely either on the beach or on their way home. I’m afraid some of your riflemen have to learn on the fly. This evacuation has been a total mess from the beginning.
What the?.. Jerry is already here!
Damn, I’ve seen this before. It looks like they’re probing our line, that means the fun is about to begin…
Watch out, enemy plane incoming! Get to cover!
We don’t have much time, bolster the line as much as you can.
Sir, with all due respect… How are we meant to hold here? We’re already running low.
I saw some crates with small arms ammunition that were left during the retreat. Take a look at them.
The engineers are still working on the vehicles. Use anything you can find in ammunition crates and don’t let them get too close to us!
Damn, we haven’t got enough AT-guns to stop all these tanks…

The retreating forces have left us a lot of rifles with cup dischargers. Their AT grenades are powerful enough to stop a tank at close quarters. We can shoot from behind fences and from buildings to ambush their vehicles.
The boys have finished! Lieutenant Shaw, retreat to the second line, I’m going to put the remainder of one of my companies under your command.
The engineers have set up a timer to blow up the vehicles. Make sure you stay well clear of them!
The vehicles are going to go up any second. Be careful.
What a waste. But I reckon it’s better than leaving them to the enemy.
Our defense has collapsed! Lieutenant Shaw, I am relieving you of your command, dismissed!
Fall back to the second line, lieutenant! Think of your men.
Watch the skies, incoming enemy planes!
Hey, look! The Brylcreem Boys decided to show up! Go get ‘em!
We should assist them somehow… Has anyone seen a functional anti-air gun?
I am afraid all of them are out of service. With a bit of luck you might repair one of them.
Excellent, that’s exactly what we need right now. This Bofors can shoot the bloody planes down.
More German planes incoming, reload the gun!
I don’t see anymore of them. Brilliant work! I bet the RAF will owe us.
Well, at least we’ve repaired this Bofors.
They just shot down one of our planes! We need to find something against these German fighters!
They’ve destroyed our fighters! We can’t count on RAF support anymore.
Sir, there are a few allied troops coming from the east! Where are they coming from?
These are the reinforcements we expected an hour ago… Use them to fill any gaps in your line.
Where the hell are you going?! There was no order for falling back!
Vessels from home are beginning to arrive. We must hold our ground to protect the evacuation.
There’s a vessel at the mole, steady on!
Another boat is at the mole, provide cover!
A transport is at the mole, keep at it!
This is the last one! We must hold a little longer while the wounded are loaded.
The Germans have reached the beach! Wipe them out before they slaughter our men at the mole!
Damn, how many of you are still out there…
Major! Greenwood, have you seen him?
We’re the last ones! Move your arse to the mole, lieutenant!
I don’t know how we made it out of there…
You fell back too early. Do not send your units too far from your first defensive line.

Victory is ours, you have done an outstanding job. This will show Jerry what we’re capable of. The invasion beaches will not be threatened by flanking attacks!
Alas there is no success to be reported. The invasion beaches will be vulnerable to counterattacks as a result, and there is little we can do to prevent that. We must try again immediately!

To protect the invasion against German flanking attacks, a couple of bridges East of the beaches must be secured.    This task has been assigned to the British 6th Airborne Brigade. They are to seize the bridge over the Caen canal and the nearby bridge over the Orne river.   Months of training proved to be invaluable as the pilot landed the glider right at the bridge over the Orne canal.    Time to spring into action! First, chase the Germans out and secure Bénouville Bridge.
You could not hold your positions.
You lost all of your units.
The pilots almost got us killed faster than Jerry could! Is everyone alright? Get your stuff and get out.
This bridge is what it’s all about. We have to capture and hold it until our reinforcements arrive.
Thank God Jerry didn't hear us landing. Let's keep it that way.
Sir, there's a pillbox up ahead. Could be a right pain. Best knock it out first.
Right, here's the plan: my section will take up positions overlooking the pillbox and provide covering fire, so your men can approach the bridge.
We're in place and ready to pin that pillbox down. Say the word.
We’ve been spotted! Everyone, open fire!
Why didn’t you wait for us?! Return fire!
Brilliant work! That pillbox is quiet.
There’s an MG on the other side! Someone take it out so we can cross the canal!
Look at ‘em legging it! Not a bad start to the morning, ha?
Smart move out there. One less headache to worry about.
The bridge is ours. Keep focused, I’m sure there will be more of them.
It seems like Jerry hasn’t rigged the bridge with explosives, I’d wager they have them stashed somewhere nearby. Let’s have a look around.
Look, some lads from the other landing zone have arrived.
One PIAT? That’s it? Are they having a laugh?!
I can tell them to turn around if you wish, Lieutenant.
I reckon it’s better than nothing. Still, this guy better treat that PIAT like it’s his firstborn.
Looks like that's the last of them. The bridge is clear, area secure, and Jerry is running away. Well done! Now back to the bridge. Squad leader’s meeting in 10.
Let’s see if there are some locals around, they might know where Jerry keeps his ammo.
MG! Hotel building, first floor, get to cover!
Heads up, anti-air spotted in the field! Knock it out so our boys in the sky can breathe easy!
We need to take out that Flak. Use a PIAT or find some explosives. Anything that we can use to disable it.
Nice one! That bloody Flak won't bother anyone again!
Check this out! I reckon these are the explosives meant for the bridge.
Not the charges... But have a look, perhaps we’ll find something handy.
Here they are! Take care of those charges. One hand grenade near the vehicle might be enough to blow it up.
Blimey, were they planning to blow up half of Normandy or what?!
Excusez-moi, monsieur... Seen any Allemania explosives? Satchels, grenades, that sort?
(French) No, no, monsieur, there must be some mistake. I am not sheltering enemies of the Reich.
Nah, mate, we're British! Tea, football, England! Aight, look... Explosives, Boche ammunition! We need that sort of a thing, you get it?

Ah, oui, oui, of course! Here small depot, but les Boches, they take it away. Dominique, mon voisin, he is résistant, watch the depot, oui? Now he is in the stable… Eh… West… Big box! Box en bois, comprendre? Wood box! He have eyes like un faucon and moustache… Long, very long, jusqu’à Marseille! Good luck, les Anglais, merci!
Alright then... Got it. Thank you, monsieur. And stay safe out there.
Reckon he means the barn west of here. There is another civvie. Sharp eyes, big moustache. Bet he knows more about the charges.
You're Dominique? Moustache down to Marseilie, eyes like falcon? Yeah, you match the description.
Oui, je suis Dominique! You are… Des soldats anglais, yes?
Monsieur, where did they take the ammo? We need the German explosives.
When you, les Anglais, you come and make noise, ze Boches, zey move ze ammo, oui? They take it... How you say... Plus loin, more far. Suivez-moi? Moi show you!
But écoutez, if ze soldats allemands are here… You shoot, d’accord?
Clear out Germans by that barn, and he'll show us where they stashed the charges.
Ça semble sûr maintenant. Come on, go with me!
The Germans will be here even sooner than you think. Set up defensive positions. Don’t let them come too close to the bridge. We do not have enough manpower to attack this riverside one more time.
They're here! Hold the line and keep them off the bridge!
I’m trying to raise sections from the other landing zones. They might be able to support us. Hold tight until then.
We did it, they’re pulling back!
Another one rollin' in! Get the PIAT! And if you’re out, find grenades or something, quick!
Well done, that'll make 'em think twice before pushing again.
I'm dry! I need a fresh mag!
We are running out of ammunition. Take a look around, you'll probably find some weapon crates left by the Germans.
A squad from another landing zone has arrived. We’ve expected the ground forces but they will work for now too. I reckon they’ve just increased our chances of holding this bridge.
Grab any ammo you can. Search the crates, buildings… Bodies… The Germans could hit us any minute.
They’ve stopped shooting. Means they’re on the move. Get ready, lads!
They’ve deployed a mortar to the northwest of us! Get rid of it before it buries all of us under this damn bridge!
The Germans are moving in from the south! Make sure this flank is secured, don’t let them surround us!
They’re pushing in from the north! Bloody hell, if they break through, that squad of ours and the entire flank are in real trouble!
Eyes on the western direction, lads! They’ve brought in an AT gun.
Just look who finally decided to show up! Commandos! These guys are as tough as they come. Now it's Jerry who's got the problem. Let's destroy the remaining attacking forces together.
We lost the Bridge! Get over there and take it back, now!
Good, the bridge is ours again. I nearly got a heart attack.
Quenching thirst at work? Since when have you become Irish?
Café Goon… Goon-dry? Christ, sounds like something you catch, not drink. Ah, Gondrée. Bloody French.
Have the Soviets really got such hats? No way they are seriously wearing furry rotten teabags on their heads.
You’re telling me they are so late because were dragging the damn orchestra?..
Gentlemen, frightfully sorry for the terrible delay. Traffic on the beaches was nothing short of murderous.
Great to see you here, your lordship. We managed so far, but now we’re at the end of our tether to be honest.

You have held this sector with remarkable resolve. An exceptional achievement indeed. I shall raise the matter of your promotion with Command. They already owe you a proper drink, preferably something French.
We’ll agree to anything spirit-based, your lordship. Even if it tastes like petrol.
But you sound dreadfully weary, gentlemen. To your good fortune, we brought some sleeping bags. Have a rest chaps, before sheer exhaustion claims you.
I reckon that’s even better than a wine. And my back… It’s so numb. Thank you, Milord.
I shan’t trouble you any longer. Worry not, we’ll take care of it.

Operation Goodwood starts today.  More than one thousand RAF heavy bombers, flying extremely low, are on their way to bomb enemy positions in Colombelles, Cagny, and a number of other villages and towns.  Thanks to the air and artillery support, progress has been good so far; you’re already miles to the south of Caen. In front lies your target for today, which is the village of Cagny.  We have no idea what the bombing attacks have achieved, or what remains of the enemy; the whole area in and around the village looks like it has been completely obliterated. Take control of the area and form a closed front to defend against any possible German counterattacks.
Any planned German counterthrust has been stopped dead in its tracks, even if our losses now prevent us from going on an all- out offensive. Have a rest, you deserve it.

This makes us look like useless bleeders! Instead of a splendid victory we’ve been routed like never before. The Germans will keep their hold on Normandy and we’re stuck in the middle of nowhere. Try again!

Battalion, listen up! Today we have to secure the town of Cagny and provide cover to assaulting mechanized convoys.
Don’t worry about Jerry, the RAF has served them bombs for breakfast.
Where the hell did they come from?!
Second wave, move out and eliminate the enemy! Remember, every phase in this operation is scheduled for a specific time.
That’s a damn bloodbath! We shouldn’t attack them in the open. This part looks like the weakest spot in the German line. We’ll have higher chances to break through there.
The AT guns on the right flank control the main road. If we destroy them, we’ll be able to request additional units.
Good, we can call in reinforcements now.
Sergeant O’Hara, I need you to assist the other vehicles. Move to the left and destroy the remaining guns!
Where the hell did they get these AT guns from? The carpet bombing should have wiped them out! Never mind. We are already behind schedule, so let’s move on.
That son of a bitch is down!
Nice hit, the bastards are dead!
Jerry is retreating to the north and digging in, which will slow down our offensive. Get rid of them as soon as possible.
The Germans have turned the entire road into a stronghold. Shit, the house-to-house clearing is gonna take the whole day…

Lucky for us, we can turn these houses into their graves. Gentlemen, I would like to introduce our demolition miracle - Churchill AVRE. Its firepower is enough to get rid of entire fortifications in the space of a few minutes.
The AVRE has arrived. Now show Jerry there is nowhere to hide!
This 230mm beast is really wild. Good work men, this road is no longer a threat to us.
The Germans have dug trenches between these hedgerows and everywhere else. Shit, this clearing is gonna take the whole day…

Lucky for us, we can literally smoke them out. Gentlemen, I would like to introduce a solution against these rats - the Churchill Crocodile. And what’s better than a flamethrower? That’s right! A bloody armoured flamethrower!
The Crocodile has arrived. Now make Jerry regret he survived the carpet bombing!
Smoking them out is definitely easier than clearing every German foxhole in the area. Good work, men.
The Germans have even more guns! Shit, we’re gonna lose so many tanks again…

Lucky for us, we finally received support against AT guns. Gentlemen, I would like to introduce the Cromwell VI. Its mobility and 95mm gun allows it to manoeuvre in close quarters and avoid the enemy's field of view.
The Cromwell has arrived. Just provide it with precise coordinates and it will take care of the rest.
Where was this Cromwell when we were attacking the first line? Could’ve saved so many lives…
The Germans have set up an entire minefield close to their positions! Shit, we’re gonna waste the whole day waiting for engineers…
Lucky for us, we have a reliable sapper. Gentlemen, I would like to introduce a solution against all minefields - the Sherman Crab. Use it for clearing up the mines.
The Crab has arrived. Now get rid of this minefield.
Perfect, these mines are no danger to us anymore. Good work, men.
Deal with the remaining Germans in the northern part of town so we can advance further.
Excellent, the northern town is ours.
And here is the air force. The most useless unit of today…
Don’t jump to conclusions. One of these planes is going in circles, he is probably scouting the area. Let’s see what enemy units he can spot.
Lots of Germans with anti-tank equipment are waiting for us. O’Hara, mark their positions so we know where exactly to expect more of these ambushes.
Damn, they’ve destroyed our special vehicle!
We are almost at the finish line. There are still some remaining German forces up ahead. I am providing you with more reinforcements so you can crush them.
The squadron we saw before reports movement of an armoured column moving in our direction. Be prepared for potential counter-attacks.
Enemy armoured vehicles to the south!
They are sending small anti-tank groups! Keep infantry close to our tanks to cover them.
The artillery is very accurate, meaning someone is spotting for their battery. O'Hara, find this observer and deal with him!
Got that damn observer! This artillery should not fire anymore.
Shit, that artillery observer got away! Don’t be surprised if there are further artillery strikes.
What the hell is that?! Has anyone seen these tanks before?
All units, load APDS! We have to destroy them!
I got one of them! Not as invincible as they look!
The second one is burning! Hell yes, we did it, men!
Just look at this thing… 150mm armor at least… We got really lucky taking it down…
I’m wondering how many of these Jerry has left. Let’s hope we don’t meet any more of them on our way.
So… Should the tank crews take a nap or something?

We’ve made it. Come on men, the bridge is not that far by now. Let’s keep moving.
Digby should have been here by now but I don’t think we can wait for him any longer. I’m afraid we will have to handle this ourselves.
Hopefully, they will reach us by morning. Till then, we must control this bridge. Lucky for us, looks like most of the Germans have gone, so we shouldn’t meet tough resistance.
The bridge is ours now. Dig in, keep watch and get some rest. Digby had better show up by morning…
This appears to be one of the tanks which attacked us during the day, let's see if it's still repairable.
Looks like we scared them to death with the tank.
Beautiful morning, Colonel Frost. I hope your kits are not completely soaked. The weather here is indeed not much different from our homelands.
Good to see you, Major. The kits are fine which I cannot say about our situation.
Thirty Corps is moving much slower than we’ve expected even in the worst case scenario. It seems like we have to be ready for all possible German counterattacks.
I believe we have everything we need, Colonel. The 6-pounders are rolling out, AT specialists looking for ambush positions.
This might not be enough, I am afraid. The enemy cannot afford to lose this bridge, otherwise their entire frontline will fall. They will throw everything they have.
This is going to be not easy for us but I am sure we will do it. The Corps has some delay but they are not that far from us. I suggest discussing the details in the HQ if you have any by far.

Listen up, lads! We are to hold this bridge until the ground forces arrive. Could be hours, could be days. No one knows. The only thing I know is that Jerry has to take this bridge brick by brick if they want it.
We’re completely surrounded, gentlemen. That simplifies our problem. Shoot everything that moves and expect enemy attacks from all directions.
Remember, this is the job we have been trained for. The eyes of the world are upon us. Let us show them what the Airborne can do.
I have always appreciated your attitude, Sir Digby. However let us not forget how short we are on supplies. Make every shot count and spare your ammo.
In case you decide to take positions in houses… For God’s sake, please watch your head while going upstairs. These bloody stairs will take us out quicker than the Germans.
Goedemorgen friends, we are the local resistance fighters. Can’t miss the chance to throw occupants off our land.
How can we assist you? We know every corner of this city and could help you either on the battlefield or go look for some ammunition and weapons.
Got it. My people will come back soon, you will not regret. We won’t let you down.
It’s an honor for us to fight back the occupiers together with you. We won’t let you down.
They are firing artillery at our positions! Take cover at our defensive positions!
We haven't got much time, make sure we are ready to meet the German forces very soon.
Is that all? I expected something more serious, not a few token infantrymen.
Those poor sods must’ve been probing our defenses.
Gentlemen, I’ve received a spot of good news. Thirty Corps and the American 82nd are advancing towards the bridge at Nijmegen. We might get relief even sooner as we thought.
Sir, if I'm correct, then the ground forces will be here in a couple hours.
The whole show hangs on what we do today. If we make it, we might just wrap up the war by Christmas. Think of the lives saved.
Everyone, take cover in basements! They are rolling out rocket artillery!
I have one of my best squads on the other side. They’ll do their best.
Let’s be very careful, these are elite troops. First, we have to distract them before they fire.
Look, the Germans have left some explosive charges here. That’s exactly what we need.
Fantastic job, people. We should get the hell out of here before their reinforcements arrive.
I cannot believe they made it… Now all the odds to hold this city are on our side!
Seems like the Corps is stuck on its way. We have to hold a little longer.
The resistance has brought us this truck. They said to take a look inside.
They will not come for us, will they?
Tell them to lower their weapons… Our fight is over…
Hold the HQ building at all costs
I'll take two - Ask the Dutch resistance squad to find more ammunition
Doomed Tea Party - Recruit the Dutch resistance squad

It’s day 5 of Market Garden, and today will decide the outcome of the entire operation.    XXX Corps has been advancing despite fierce German counterattacks on the motorway they’re using, which has already been dubbed 'Hell’s Highway'.    Despite the constant counterattacks from east and west of the highway, you’ve advanced all the way to Nijmegen.    Unfortunately, we have no intel on German strength and position in the area, so we should start moving forward and find out where they are ourselves. The Paratroopers are waiting for us at the very next bridge, just 7 miles away. Let’s go!

You’ve done the king proud! This will surely earn a mention in dispatches. The entire operation seems doomed, but now at least we can push on and give Market Garden one last chance; we will see what happens next. Splendid soldiering!

Too bad, commander! The Germans reacted more efficiently than we expected, putting the entire operation at risk. We should have found a way through the German positions but we didn’t, who’s going to tell General Horrocks?
That borders on disaster. We failed to secure a win, you need to go back and get another effort going!
Punch a hole in the enemy position and drive north!
Welcome back to the front line, Lieutenant! This is north bridgehead, it must remain in our control!
Operation Market Garden is in critical phase, push towards Arnhem must be attempted at all costs!
Be quick, be decisive, and try not to lose too many men! Use the terrain to your advantage.
More reinforcements will become available as you progress with your assault!
Gentlemen! Germans are close to our Field HQ!
We must hold our command post! There is no room for surrender!
Americans from 82nd Airborne are bogged down ahead! Let's help them out.
Good to see you, Lieutenant! We didn't think we'd make it! Our men are under your command.
Major! Now you can request an airstrike.
Secret objective #1: Wicked! - incinerated enemy soldiers
Secret objective #2: Tamed the cat! - captured German panther.

Everything that could have gone wrong in this operation went horribly wrong. Just now, we’ve again suffered horrendous casualties, but you’ve managed to make it out of there and live to fight another day. Market Garden failed due to ignorant commanders, not through a lack of courage.

This is awful, they gave us a right pasting. Operation Market Garden has failed, and now our retreat has failed as well. Now you have become a prisoner of war. Perhaps this was just one bridge too far?

You have been in battle for 3 days straight, while the situation is getting worse for the British paratroopers in and around Arnhem.  Since the resupply operation failed, things are getting worse by the minute.  Controlling the bridge has become impossible. XXX corps is still south of Nijmegen, fighting to get control over the bridge there. It doesn’t look like they will break through soon.  The units fighting west of the bridge are to retreat from Arnhem to the town of Oosterbeek. That includes you. Pick up any stragglers you might find and make sure you stay out of the hands of the Germans.
You lost all of your units.
The evacuation team has left without you.
That makes two of us, mate…
Cholerny Szwaby… Look at them, no shame, huh? They already dare to crawl this close to us.
You alive, yes? Good. Though, you look like ghosts, and… Boże święty, you smell like you've been buried already.

I have one good news… and one very shitty one. Good news is that you caught your last train out of this hell. Me and my squad, well, just the two of us left now, we look for poor boys like you to drag out.

The bad news is, if you take a quick look around… We’re surrounded by these skurwiele. Either we find more weapons and send Szwaby back in pieces where they came from, or activate our brains and slip past the patrols. Lucky for us, the night is dark today.
So… what do you say, huh? We find more guns and send them back to their Vaterland, or the clever way, like ghosts in the night?
Hold! An enemy vehicle coming from the south-east.
Watch out! An enemy vehicle coming from the south-east.
Szwaby are attacking the British outpost! We need to help our people.
Things became even worse. I recall the last outpost controlled by Brits was three hundred meters away from here. The rats are increasing their pressure and are not giving up.
I’ll be damned! Kowalczyk, you made it out again! Bloody glad to see you, mate! I am really wondering how you manage to escape death every time.
There’s no special secret, actually. I just say “not today” to this insatiable bastard.
Thanks God you lads are still holding this position. Major sent us to support you.
So you’re our reinforcements?.. That’s all?.. Cholera, Major is losing his sense of humor if it’s supposed to be some kind of a joke.
A bloody tank from the east incoming! Our PIAT operator got hit. Lads, grab his launcher and destroy the tank!
O cholera… That’s a flamethrower tank! Kill it now!
Nice hit, lads! Let them taste their own weapon.
I reckon that’s all of them… At least for now. So if you’ll excuse me, gentlemen, I better disappear before the Major completely loses his mind over how long I’ve been gone.
I need to report to Major Urquhart about my return. He should be at HQ, in the hotel.
Do you even realise what you’ve done?! The CO will have our heads if he sees this mess!
Still, it might be worth looking around. Maybe some lads could use a hand.
I heard you people are arguing about something?
Just look what those idiots have done! Blew up the damn building and the wreckage landed right on the wheel of our 17-pounder!
Major say destroy. We destroy, tak?! We scream “Move away”. You stand like stupid cow and talk to wind!
Calm down, both of you. It’s not the right time to piss each other. Why can't you just replace the wheel?

Well… There’s one option, technically… Back on manoeuvres, we saw some wasted Canadians try swapping a 17-pounder wheel with one off a captured Opel Blitz. Sort of a wager. Looked ridiculous, and the wheel fell to bits after two minutes of towing.
Do you think you'll get it done?
Worked for a bunch of drunk Canucks, why not us? Just get us the bloody wheel off one of those captured trucks and we’ll take care of the rest.
Dobrze, let’s search for a szwabski truck.
No way… You actually found it! Gov, give us a hand, will you?
I say, bloody hell, she made it! The wheel's gone, but who cares? This is the gun’s last stop anyway. We’re not dragging her out during evac. You’ve done us a real favour, mate.
Don’t even think about nicking it. I know your type, Polak. What do you want?
Relax, I don’t need the whole thing. Just… Part of it. More specifically, I need the wheel. Can you take it off for me?

What the hell do you need a wheel for? …Eh, never mind. I could do it. But let’s say I’d be willing… for a very particular kind of trade. Couple of days back, we were pushing toward Arnhem and I got hit by shrapnel.
Thought my lungs exploded. There was a medic who jabbed a syringe in me and the pain just… Vanished. Now it’s the only thing that keeps me from screaming every time I move.
We are running short on morphine but I think I know where you might get some. Jerry has a supply stash not far from here. It’s in a broken down ammo trailer near the entrance.
Can you lend me one of your Jeeps to tow it out?
Hell no. That trailer might go up any second, and the Major said no risking the transport. We still need to get our arses out of here. But if you find anything usable in there, bring it here.
That’s the lorry I am looking for. Let’s try our luck talking to the mechanic.
This trailer is still loaded with ammunition, I have to be careful.
The red tractor over there might help me to tow the trailer.
Cholera… The tank is empty. Need to find petrol to refuel it.
Should be enough fuel for now.
Now we talk. This thing is capable of towing light emplacements.
It won’t budge, the wheel is damaged. Maybe I could tow this thing away.
Świetnie, now I can the reach Szwaby's treasure.
Good, now I can bring this wheel to the artillerymen.
Think that’s all. Let’s report to the Major now.
Dziękuję… Ah… Bedankt… It is very good eating. And I really like how beautiful here around. Even my hometown did not look so good before the war as your bombed town right now.
At ease, lieutenant. Good to see you back in one piece.

We received tragic news while you were away. The garrison of Lieutenant Colonel Frost in Arnhem had capitulated. I am afraid we shall not wait for anyone from that city to reach us. To avoid their fate, I have made a decision to evacuate our people tonight.

We will move out under cover of darkness to avoid unnecessary attention. You are needed in a recon role, Lieutenant. The Polish forces with boats are going to wait for you at the river. You have to meet them and give us a signal to begin the evacuation.
We are going to put an end to this folly operation we call Market Garden and save our wounded and starved men. In the meantime…
That mortar’s coming from the next district over. Damn things's got a clear line on us.
We need it silenced before it reduces this hotel to rubble. Move swiftly.
Lieutenant Kowalczyk, you’ve got some of your countrymen without a unit. They’re yours now. Make good use of them.
Good. One problem off the board.
Heads up, they’re pushing through from the east. Lieutenant, I need you on that flank. We have reserves nearby, but without support, they won’t hold.
They have decided to go full scale, ha? Hold your ground, people!
O, kurwa… Tiger is coming from the north, take care of it!
You gave us a hand with the 17-pounder. Now it’s our turn. At your command, Lieutenant.
A second Tiger? Ja pierdolę… Szwaby must having a laugh.
We did it men, they are falling back. Hopefully that was their last attack for today. Get some rest. The Major said we are moving out tonight.
…No way she treated you like that! The hell she’s thinking she is?
Well… Women… Can’t live with ‘em, can’t live without ‘em.
The break is over, lads. We have to move to the finish line.
Our Polish friends are still waiting for us to arrive at the shore to get us out of here. We lost contact with them this evening and they probably don’t even know we’re still alive.
They won’t be waiting for too long for us, Szwaby are pushing them just as bad as they do to us. We have to let them know we’re still here as soon as possible. It’s now or never.
The Szwaby are in the village! Don’t waste time on killing all of them, we have to hurry! Our primary objective is to let the people on the other side know we’re still alive!
Sir?.. There’s no one there… The bloody evac team is not there!

Lieutenant, we've finally made contact with the evacuation team. They’re still holding, but had to pull back east under pressure. There’s a village nearby crawling with German vehicles. If we don’t act fast, they’ll compromise the entire operation.
The evac team won’t last much longer. Those vehicles must be taken out as soon as possible. That’s your priority, Lieutenant Kowalczyk.
The village is swarming with infantry as well. I’m sending a platoon your way, they’ll draw attention from the enemy. Focus on knocking out those damn vehicles.

I wish I could give you more. But these are the last combat-ready men we’ve got. Remember what you're fighting for. Behind you are dozens of wounded, starving men who haven’t slept in days. You’re their last chance, Lieutenant. I trust you. Don’t let them down.
All vehicles destroyed! Let’s get the fuck out of here!
How is this thing still even driving without wheels and transmission? Szwaby should have rather made that many civilian cars instead of tanks.
Two vehicles down but we have to get rid of them faster!
Three out of four! One to go!
Where do you think you’re going?! We have a job to do!
That’s the last cab. Everyone, get on the board! Hope we didn’t leave someone behind.
Bloody hell, get us out of here! They're already waiting!
Oi, wait for us, you bastards!
We’re almost there. But we should not leave our men behind.
Good, we made it through. Let’s get the hell out.
Half of the town is in flames. Let’s avoid these spots and sneak through patrols like shadows.
We should not leave the corpses, other Szwaby will find them.
This skurwiel saw the body! Kill him now!
Cholera, they see us. Open fire!
I think it was the last of them. Let’s keep moving, chlopaki.
